The Psalmist reproves those who do not wish to understand their offenses. In reproving rather than denying this, he sings: “Who understands offenses?” As he says in Psalm CVI: “Who is wise and understands these things?” so here too: “Who understands offenses?”

We often call rashness firmness, and call injury freedom; we give folly the name of simplicity, and call flattery perfect charity. Give the eye that searches the heart to these matters, and it will understand them. Therefore the one who understands cries out: “Cleanse me, O Lord, from my hidden faults,” because even those things that are thought holy in me are subject to guilt. “And spare your servant from the offenses of [Col. 0350B] others,” to which we provide fuel by flattering them.

For if they do not rule over me through flattery, then I shall be blameless and clean from the greatest offense. But when I speak without flattery, then the words of my mouth will please you. Then the meditation of my heart will always be in your presence.

For the one who does not flatter thinks of nothing except this: that he is not afraid to see God. Therefore he speaks freely to God, and his words please him; the meditation of his heart is in the presence of God. To this person he says: “My helper and my redeemer,” who reigns for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XIX

For the end; a psalm of David.

May the Lord hear you on the day of tribulation; may the name of the God of Jacob protect [Col. 0350C] you. May he send you help from the sanctuary, and may he defend you from Zion. May he remember all your sacrifice, and may your burnt offering become fat. May he grant you according to your heart and confirm all your counsel.

We shall rejoice in your salvation, and in the name of the Lord our God we shall be magnified. May the Lord fulfill all your petitions. Now I know that the Lord has saved his anointed. He will hear him from his holy heaven; salvation is in the powers of his right hand.

Some trust in chariots and others in horses, but we shall call upon the name of the Lord our God. They were bound and fell, but we have risen and stood upright. O Lord, save the king, and hear us on the day when we call upon you.

## COMMENTARY

To Christ going to the cross, the Church says:

[Col. 0350D] “May the Lord hear you on the day of tribulation”—to the man who offered himself as redemption for all. “May your burnt offering become fat”: the offering that you make on the altar of the cross. May he confirm all your counsel in such a way that we may rejoice in your salvation and call upon you in the name of the Lord our God when you have risen from the dead.

For the Lord saves his anointed, and the salvation of his right hand will be in the powers, so that he may lead the thief at his right hand into paradise. Some trust in chariots, others in horses, but we shall be magnified in the name of the Lord our God. When they fall, we shall rise, because our king has been saved; rising from the dead, he ascended into heaven, and, seated at the right hand of God [Col. 0351A] the Father, he hears us on the day when we call upon him. To him be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XX

For the end; a psalm of David.

O Lord, the king will rejoice in your strength, and he will exult greatly in your salvation. You granted him the desire of his heart, and you did not deprive him of the will of his lips. For you went before him with blessings of sweetness; you placed upon his head a crown of precious stone.

He asked one thing from you; you granted it to him, and length of days for ever and ever. Great is his glory in your salvation; you will place glory and great beauty upon him. For you will give him as a blessing for ever and ever; you will gladden him with joy in your presence.

For the king hopes in the Lord, and in the mercy of the Most High he will not be shaken. Let your hand be found by all your enemies; let your right hand find all those who hate you. You will place them like a fiery oven at the time of your presence. The Lord will trouble them in his anger, and fire will devour them. You will destroy their fruit from the earth and their seed from among the children of men.

For they turned evil things against you; they devised plans that they could not establish. For you will make them turn their backs; in what remains of you, you will prepare their face. Be exalted, O Lord, in your strength; we shall sing and praise your mighty acts.

## COMMENTARY

Here he calls a perfect person a king—not one who rejoices in his own strength, but one who rejoices in the strength of him who took him up, who granted him the desire of his heart [Col. 0351C] and did not deprive him of the will of his lips. For he went before him with the blessing of sweetness. He is sweet to one who loves his commandments, and he commands as he said above: “More than honey and the honeycomb to my mouth” (Psalm XVIII).

Therefore the blessing of sweetness is his body: “Taste,” he says, “and see how sweet the Lord is” (Psalm XXXIII). When he says, “You have placed a crown upon his head,” Paul, the imitator of Christ, calls those who embraced Christ’s exhortations his joy and his crown (Philippians IV). Because the apostles gloried in his glory, it is said of them: “A crown was placed upon the Lord’s head,” made of precious stone, as the prophecy of Ezekiel and the Apocalypse of John declare.

“He asked one thing”: he is speaking of the assumed man. Having been placed in death, he received life, and the length of his days extends not [Col. 0351D] to old age, but for ever and ever. “Great is his glory.” In what does it consist? Not in the arrogance of divinity, but in the salvation of humanity. Therefore you will place glory and great beauty upon him and give him in eternal blessing, because he thus hoped in the Lord and was not shaken in his mercy, so that for the salvation of the human race he even permitted himself to be sacrificed.

From this point the Father speaks to the Son: “Let your hand be found by all your enemies”—your right hand, the one that received nails on the cross. Let that hand find those who hate you. “Place them like a fiery oven at the time of your presence.” Then in your anger you will trouble them, and fire will devour them.

For when the day of judgment comes, the fruit of those who persist in unbelief will perish from the [Col. 0352A] earth. He causes those whom he received as sown in death to bear fruit in the resurrection—for the Apostle proves that our bodies are sown when he says: “It is sown in corruption; it rises in incorruption” (1 Corinthians XV). But those who turn evil things against Christ, as the Jews did then, and devise a plan of perversity against him, will on that day be placed on their backs, and in what remains he will prepare their faces.

This means that they do not rise with the saints in the first resurrection, but in what remained after the first resurrection he will prepare their faces. Then, praising the Lord Jesus Christ and offering a hymn, we shall sing these words and say to him: “Be exalted, O Lord, in your strength.” No longer do you overshadow your strength in the concealment of a servant’s person; be exalted in your strength, and let those who hesitate to believe that you are our Savior perceive [Col. 0352B] you as avenger. To you be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXI

For the end; a psalm of David, for the morning reception.

My God, my God, look upon me; why have you forsaken me? The words of my offenses are far from my salvation. My God, I shall cry out by day, and you will not hear; and by night, yet not for my folly. But you dwell in the holy place, the praise of Israel.

Our fathers hoped in you; they hoped, and you delivered them. They cried out to you and were saved; they hoped in you and were not put to shame. But I am a worm and not a man, the reproach of men and the outcast of the people. All who saw me mocked me; they spoke with their lips and shook their heads.

“He hoped in the Lord; let him rescue him. Let him save him, since he desires him.” [Col. 0352C]

For you are the one who drew me from the womb; my hope from my mother’s breasts. Upon you I was cast from the womb; from my mother’s womb you are my God. Do not depart from me, for tribulation is near, and there is no one to help.

Many calves surrounded me; fat bulls besieged me. They opened their mouth against me like a ravening and roaring lion. I was poured out like water, and all my bones were scattered. My heart became like wax melting in the midst of my belly. My strength dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue cleaved to my jaws; you brought me down into the dust of death.

For many dogs surrounded me; the assembly of the wicked besieged me. They pierced my hands and my feet; they counted all my bones. They themselves watched and examined me; they divided my garments among [Col. 0352D] themselves, and upon my clothing they cast lots.

But you, O Lord, do not keep your help far from me; look upon me for my defense. Rescue my soul from the sword, O God, and my only one from the hand of the dog. Save me from the lion’s mouth and my humility from the horns of the unicorns.

I shall declare your name to my brothers; in the midst of the Church I shall praise you. You who fear the Lord, praise him; glorify him, all the seed of Jacob. Let all the seed of Israel fear him, because he has not despised or scorned the prayer of the poor. He did not turn his face from me, and when I cried out to him, he heard me.

With you is my praise in the great church; I shall fulfill my vows in the presence of those who fear him. The poor will eat and be filled, and those who seek the Lord [Col. 0353A] will praise him; their hearts will live for ever.

All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord. All the families of the nations will worship in his presence. For the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he himself will rule the nations. All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and worshiped; in his presence all who descend into the earth will fall.

And my soul will live for him, and my seed will serve him. The coming generation will be announced to the Lord, and they will announce his righteousness to the people who will be born, whom the Lord has made.

## COMMENTARY
While the Lord was undergoing his Passion, he explained the mysteries of this psalm. For, expressing the first verse of this psalm in Hebrew words, he expounded the remaining verses that followed. For there we read the Pharisees saying: “He trusted in the Lord; let him deliver him; let him save him, since he desires him.” In his Passion, many young bulls surrounded him—that is, the Jewish people. Fat bulls besieged him—that is, the chief priests. They opened their mouths against him, saying: “He has blasphemed” (Matt. XXIX, 65). They uttered a roar like a lion that seizes and growls. That condemnable man Caiaphas, the chief priest, roared in such a way that he even tore his garments.

“Like water poured out are my bones.” He appropriately used the image of water, because the body of Christ knows nothing except how to wash away sins. “My heart has become like melting wax within my belly.” When wax has been dissolved by fire, it does not perish, as other substances, once consumed by fire, are reduced to ashes; wax, however, when it has burned, returns to what it was. Knowing, therefore, that he could not perish, he says: “Like wax, my heart has melted within my belly.”

“My strength has dried up like a potsherd.” He did not say, “It has been broken like a potsherd,” for although its breaking is irreparable, its firing is found to be praiseworthy. Accordingly, the more thoroughly the potter’s work has dried, the better and more solid it is found to be. Thus my strength dried up in the fire of tribulation, like a potsherd.

“And my tongue has clung to my jaws.” Remaining silent like a defendant, with bowed head, I did not repel the false witnesses in the presence of the judge; they led me down into the dust of death. “And many dogs surrounded me.” In this way they besieged me in their wicked assembly that they dug through my hands and feet and counted all my bones. They themselves also examined and looked upon me, and divided my garments among themselves, and cast lots for my clothing (John XIX).

I do not know with what presumption of spirit you sing the Psalter in your synagogues, O most wicked Jews. Consider, wretched men, that this is the Lord whom you denied, and at least now, fearing the Lord: “Praise him, all the seed of Jacob; glorify him. Fear him, all the seed of Israel.” For he does not reject your prayer—to such an extent that, while hanging on the cross, he prayed for those crucifying him—so that his praise might be in the great Church and that he might fulfill his vows before those who fear him.

While the poor in spirit eat his body so that they may be satisfied, and, having become rich, praise the Lord in faith as they seek him, their heart will live forever. Through them all the ends of the earth will be converted to the Lord [Col. 0354A], so that not Judaea alone but all the lands of the nations may worship in his presence; for the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he himself will rule the nations.

Behold, Christ’s school has been celebrated among poor disciples. Now, school of the Pharisees, rise and see those eating! And those who ate ate and were satisfied, and praised the Lord as they sought him. But these ate, and all the rich of the earth worshiped. Therefore, in the presence of God, all who descend into the earth will fall. For earthly descent serves human beings; but may our soul serve God and live for him.

May our seed serve him in the sanctification of continence, so that we may announce to the Lord the generation that is to come—that is, so that we may contemplate the future glory of the saints. And may we announce the justice of God to our brothers and to the son in age [the reading is uncertain], and to every people that will be born, whom the Lord our God has made, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXII

### A Psalm of David

The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing; he has placed me in a pastureland. He has led me beside the water of refreshment; he has restored my soul. He has led me along paths of righteousness for his name’s sake. For even if I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, because you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they have comforted me. You have prepared a table before me, against those who afflict me. You have anointed my head with oil, and how exceedingly splendid is my intoxicating cup! And your mercy will pursue me all the days [Col. 0354C] of my life. And I shall dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days.

## COMMENTARY

In the twenty-first psalm we had the tribulation of the Passion; in the twenty-second psalm let us receive the joy of the resurrection, so that, since there we sowed the tears of the suffering Lord, here we may reap the joys of the risen Lord.

Let those who wish say: “My field will shepherd me, and I shall lack nothing.” Let another say: “My business will shepherd me,” or “my military service,” or “my industry,” or “my craft,” or “my studies,” “and I shall lack nothing.” Let us say with the Church: “The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing.”

This expression, then, belongs to one who despises possessions if he has them, or does not wish to have them if he does not have them. Otherwise the person who desires something else in his prayer is lying in the song. For if he strives so that earthly works of whatever kind may shepherd him, he does not say with complete integrity, “The Lord shepherds me.”

This, therefore, is the voice of the perfect, which the Church has received from the Lord’s Passion: placed in pastures and led beside the water of refreshment. For wherever a spring abounds and flows forth through generous channels, there are greenness, beauty, and refreshment. These things will happen to me because through his Passion he has restored my soul.

“He has led me along paths of righteousness for his name’s sake. For even if I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I shall no longer fear evil, because you are with me, who have subjected the dominion of death.”

Let us now see what the Church contains within herself. She has a rod with which she threatens the delinquent. She has a staff with which she aids the penitent. She has a table from which she gives bread to the believer. She has oil with which she anoints the head of one who confidently claims the liberty of conscience. She has a cup with which she intoxicates those preaching the word, so that, when it is the third hour of the day, that person may already be considered drunk in his preaching.

She has the mercy of God, which follows him throughout all the days of his life, so that he may dwell in the house of the Lord for the length of his days, praising the Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXIII

### A Psalm of David for the first day of the week

The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness, the world and all who dwell in it. For he founded it upon the seas and prepared it upon the rivers. Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, or who shall stand in his holy place? The one innocent in hands and pure in heart, who has not received his soul in vain and has not sworn deceitfully against his neighbor. He shall receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.

This is the generation of those who seek the face of the God of Jacob. Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, O eternal doors, and the King of glory shall enter. Who is this King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty in battle. Lift up your gates, O princes, and be lifted up, O eternal doors, and the King of glory shall enter. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts—he is the King of glory.

## COMMENTARY

The twenty-third psalm, at its entrance, placed above its very threshold the title “for the first day of the week.” On that day the Lord said, “Let there be light” (Gen. I); on it man ate the bread of angels (Ps. LXXVII); on it the Lord himself rose from the dead.

This day is placed in the title because it itself won possession of the earth which, in the beginning, he had made—the world and all who dwell in it. But if you ask how he won it, the answer is: through water and the Holy Spirit.

Therefore he names the enclosed seas as the one basin of all waters, because just as all rivers have this one basin, so all have one and the same Holy Spirit. In him human beings become innocent in hands and pure in heart. And whoever has not entered there receives his soul in vain, provided that he has not sworn deceitfully against his neighbor, because through the gift of baptism the Holy Spirit becomes his neighbor.

Through him he promises to renounce the devil and all his pomps. To swear, therefore, is to establish a right by which what has been renounced is abstained from and what has been promised is kept. This person has not sworn deceitfully against his neighbor: how has he become a neighbor of the Holy Spirit? Because the one who was far away has been brought near. And the one who has been brought near swore to this neighbor when he received blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.

And he became a son of God among the generation of those who seek the Lord and seek the face of the God of Jacob. To him it is now said: “Lift up the gates of your prince.” Cast away the example of Adam, who is your prince according to the flesh, and be lifted up, O eternal doors, possessing the King of glory, powerful and strong, and powerful in battle, conquering vices and their nurturers, wicked spirits [Col. 0356A].

“Lift up, therefore, the gates of your prince.” As we have borne the image of the earthly, let us also bear the image of the heavenly (1 Cor. XV). Who is this King of glory? Christ, the Son of God—he is the King of glory, excluding the prince of disgrace.

When the temples of the idols had been cast down, as though they were the gates of the devil’s prince, he lifted up the eternal gates of the holy Catholic Church, in which the King of glory reigns. If you ask who this King of glory is, the Apostle will answer: the King of all unto salvation, Christ the Son of God, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXIV

### A Psalm of David. For the end.

To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul; my God, I trust in you; I shall not be put to shame. Nor may my enemies mock me; for all who wait for you shall not be confounded. Let all who act wickedly be confounded in vain.

Make your ways known to me, Lord, and teach me your paths. Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are God my Savior, and I have waited for you all day. Remember your mercies, Lord, and your compassion, which are from eternity. Do not remember the sins of my youth or my ignorances. According to your mercy, remember me, because of your goodness, Lord.

The Lord is sweet and upright; therefore he will give a law to sinners on the way. He will guide the meek in judgment; he will teach the humble his ways. All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth for those who seek his covenant and his testimonies.

For your name’s sake, Lord, you will be gracious toward my sin, for it is great. Who is the person who fears the Lord? He will establish a law for him on the way he has chosen. His soul will dwell amid good things, and his seed will inherit the earth.

The Lord is a firm and secure support for those who fear him, and his covenant is given so that it may be revealed to them. My eyes are always toward the Lord, because he himself will draw my feet out of the snare.

Look upon me and have mercy on me, because I am alone and poor. The tribulations of my heart have multiplied; deliver me from my distresses. See my humiliation and my labor, and forgive all my sins.

Look upon my enemies, for they have multiplied, and they hate me with unjust hatred. Guard my soul and deliver me; I shall not be put to shame, because I have hoped in you. The innocent and upright have adhered to me, because I have waited for you.

Deliver Israel, O God, from all its tribulations.

## COMMENTARY

Withdrawing my soul from all earthly profits and from everything in this world that appears good, I have lifted it to you, Lord. I no longer trust in money, in a house, in business, in military service, or in possessions; trusting in you, I ask not to be put to shame when I depart from the body, because there is eternal confusion there.

Let not my enemies mock me there, because those who await you alone, having despised everything else, will not be confounded. There the wicked and those who do what is vain will be confounded.

And since, with you as guide, Lord, one reaches life, make known to me your ways, which you yourself walked, so that I may walk along them, and teach me your paths, so that I may proceed on them. And so that I may do this, guide me in your truth, and teach me, for you are God my Savior. For I endure no one besides you all day—that is, every day.

Remember, Lord, your mercies, which are from eternity; and just as you have been merciful to all, so also be merciful to me, so that you may not remember the sins of my youth and my ignorances. Rather, according to your great mercy, remember me, lest I perish through my bitterness, not because of my merits but because you yourself are sweet and upright.

All your ways are mercy and truth for those who seek your covenant and your testimonies. I ask, therefore, that you be gracious toward my sin, for it is great. For this reason I have despised my own way and chosen your way, and I have lifted my soul to you, so that my soul may dwell amid good things and my seed may possess that land—a land which the dragon has not devoured, which is not the bosom of the dead, which does not produce thorns, but in which the Lord is the support of those who fear him, and the testimony that it may be revealed to them [Col. 0357B].

And because a snare is set by the enemy for those who desire these things: “My eyes are always toward the Lord, because he himself will draw my feet out of the snare.” “Look upon me and have mercy on me, because I am alone and poor.”

Everyone who applies himself more intensely to lamentation and prayer is alone and poor. His heart’s tribulations multiply as he remembers everything that is done in the world, and he cries out to be freed from the world’s distresses. Therefore he says: “See my humiliation and my labor, and forgive all my sins.”

“Look upon my enemies,” he says, “because they have multiplied; with unjust hatred they hate me.” Demons persecute the one who is humble before God and assail him with unjust hatred.

Therefore he says: “Guard my soul and rescue me, so that I may not be confounded, because I hope in you. May the innocent and upright adhere to me, because I wait for you, Lord, who deliver Israel from all its straits.”

Now whoever adheres to the innocent and upright and waits for the Lord becomes Israel—that is, “seeing God.” And therefore, having become Israel, he is redeemed from all his straits, through our Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXV

### A Psalm of David

Judge me, Lord, for I have walked in my innocence, and, hoping in the Lord, I shall not be shaken. Test me, Lord, and try me; burn my kidneys and my heart. For your mercy is before my eyes, and I have been pleased with your truth.

I have not sat with the council of vanity, and I shall not enter with those who do iniquity. I have hated the assembly of the wicked, and I shall not sit with the impious. I shall wash my hands among the innocent, and I shall surround your altar, Lord, so that I may hear the voice of praise and recount all your wonders.

Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place where your glory dwells. Do not destroy my soul with the impious, nor my life with men of blood, in whose hands are iniquities and whose right hand is filled with gifts.

But I have walked in my innocence; redeem me and have mercy on me. For my foot has stood on the straight path; in the Churches I will bless you, Lord.

## COMMENTARY

“Judge me, Lord”: I would not have dared to say this unless your mercy were before my eyes. Certain, therefore, that your judgments assist me, I have dared to say, “Judge me.”

These two things give the Christian confidence: to have the mercy of God before his eyes and to be pleased with the truth of the Catholic faith; not to sit in the council of heretics, but to wash his hands among Catholics so that he may surround the Lord’s altar, where he may hear the voice of praise, recount all God’s wonders, and say to the Lord:

“When I depart from the body, do not destroy my soul with the impious, because I have loved the beauty of your house and hated the assemblies of the wicked. Let not my life perish with men of blood, those who, sitting in judgment, accepted gifts in order to pervert judgment” [Col. 0358B].

“For I have harmed no one in judgment; redeem me and have mercy on me. My foot has stood on the straight way, in the true faith. In the Churches I will bless the Lord, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.”

## PSALM XXVI

### A Psalm of David. For the end, before he was anointed.

The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life; from whom shall I tremble? When evildoers draw near against me to devour my flesh, those who afflict me, my enemies, they themselves have grown weak and fallen.

Though armies encamp against me, my heart shall not fear. Though battle rise up against me, in this I shall hope. One thing I have asked of the Lord; this I shall seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life [Col. 0358C], that I may see the Lord’s will and visit his temple.

For he has hidden me in his tabernacle; on the day of evils he has protected me in the hiding-place of his tabernacle. He has exalted me upon a rock, and now he has lifted up my head above my enemies.

I have gone around and sacrificed in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation; I will sing and make a psalm to the Lord. Hear, Lord, my voice with which I have cried to you; have mercy on me and hear me.

My heart has said to you, “My face has sought you”; “Your face, Lord, I shall seek.” Do not turn your face away from me; do not turn away in anger from your servant. Be my helper; do not abandon me or despise me, God my Savior.

For my father and my mother have abandoned me, but the Lord has taken me up. Establish a law for me, Lord, on your way, and guide me on a straight path because of my enemies.

Do not hand me over to the souls of those who afflict me, for unjust witnesses have risen against me, and iniquity has lied against itself. I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.

Wait for the Lord; act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord.

## COMMENTARY

The title of the psalm says, “Before he was anointed.” It is customary for a person placed in power to remember what he did when he was poor. Therefore, before he was anointed, he remembers, already anointed, and sets out what his thought had been before his anointing, in this order—as though he were saying:

“If, before I was anointed, my seven brothers, great men, were rejected from anointing, and God took care of me so that he might choose and anoint the small and insignificant one [Col. 0359A], now that he himself enlightens me and drives darkness away from me, whom shall I fear? With him defending me, from whom shall I tremble?

“Even if those sent by Saul draw near me to devour my flesh—those who afflict me, and my enemies—they themselves have grown weak and fallen. Even if battle rises up against me, I shall hope in the Lord’s illumination.

“This is the one thing I ask of the Lord and seek: to see what pleases the Lord, to know his will, and to see his temple protected, so that whoever takes refuge in him may be honored and cannot be snatched from the hands of his enemies.

“May the Church of God possess such reverence that it is honored even by its enemies, so that I may be hidden in his tabernacle on the day of evils, exalted upon the rock, so that the gates of hell may not prevail against it; so that its head may be lifted above its enemies [Col. 0359B]; and so that I may go around and sacrifice in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation, sing in it, and praise the Lord. Pouring out prayers there, I shall confidently say to the Lord, ‘Have mercy on me and hear me.’

“Provided, however, that, showing himself a lover of God, he cries out invisibly to the Invisible One. ‘Moses,’ he says, ‘was silent with his mouth but cried out in his heart’; hence the Lord said to him, ‘Why do you cry out to me?’ (Exod. XIV).

“So also in this place the lover of God, seeking no appearance of the world but desiring only the beauty of Christ, cries out in the language of the heart those words which lovers customarily speak with their tongues to those whom they love, saying: ‘My heart has said to you, I have sought your face. Do not turn your face away from me; do not turn away in anger from your servant.’

“For I have done such things that you may justly be angry and turn away from my desire. Yet, since you are merciful and my helper, do not abandon me or despise me, God my Savior.”

Consider what sort of love he offers to God. We read: “A man will leave father and mother and cling to his wife” (Gen. II; Matt. XIX). So here, because he loved the Lord, he says: “My father and my mother have abandoned me, but the Lord has taken me up”—as though he were saying, “You, O Lord, have taken up the one abandoned by his parents.”

“Establish a law for me on your way; show me what you desire, what you do not desire, what you love, and what you hate. For it could happen that, in my desire to obey, I might offend if I do not first learn how I ought to act.

“And because my enemies are concerned with nothing else except that, once you are offended, they may have power over me, I ask this: guide me on the straight way because of my enemies, so that you may not hand me over to the souls of those who persecute me, for unjust witnesses have risen against me.

“They display the beauty of the world, which, though mortal in its taste, is attractive in appearance and deceives the observer with a false face. But I, who despise these things, believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land—not of mortals, but of the living.”

To this the Spirit responded in the antiphon: “If, then, you believe that you will see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living, wait for the Lord; act manfully, let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord, who reigns forever and ever.” Amen.

## PSALM XXVII

### A Psalm of David

To you, Lord, I will cry; my God, do not be silent toward me, lest you at some time be silent toward me and I become like those descending into the pit. Hear, Lord, the voice of my supplication when I pray to you, when I lift up my hands toward your holy temple.

Do not hand me over together with sinners, and do not destroy me with those who practice iniquity, who speak peace with their neighbor but evil is in their hearts. Give them according to their works and according to the wickedness of their inventions. According to the works of their hands, deal with them; repay them their recompense.

For they have not understood the works of the Lord, and in the works of their hands you will destroy them; you will not build them up. Blessed is the Lord, for he has heard the voice of my supplication.

The Lord is my helper and my protector; in him my heart has hoped, and I have been helped. My flesh has blossomed again, and according to my will I will confess to him. The Lord is the strength of his people and the protector of the salvations of his Christ.

Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance; shepherd them and lift them up forever.

## COMMENTARY

In the Son of God we confess a perfect God and a perfect human being. In this psalm we recognize him addressing his inner self, in which he cries out that he not be handed over together with sinners, although he committed no sin (1 Pet. II).

And because there was never deceit in his mouth, he prays that, although he will become like those descending into the pit—that is, when he becomes like the buried—he may not have a share with those who speak peace with their mouths but devise evil in their hearts, as Judas did.

“Give them,” he says, “according to their works.” They did not understand the works of the Lord, and, although they saw him raising the dead, they said: “This man is not from God” (John IX). But Jesus said to them: “If you do not believe my words, believe at least the works” (John X).

They, however, did not understand the works of the Lord, and therefore they will be destroyed and not built up, because the Lord raised Jesus from the dead; his flesh blossomed again, and according to his will he confessed to him. For everything he suffered, he suffered according to his will, as he himself says: “I have power to lay down my life and to take it up again” (John X). Therefore he says: “According to my will I will confess to him.”

For he is the strength of his people, because he fulfilled his words by his deeds. He said that he would suffer, and he suffered; that he would die, and he died; that he would rise, and he rose from the dead, removing the weakness of fear and giving the strength of a most ready will [Col. 0360D].

For he is the protector of the salvations of his Christ: undoubtedly, the one who is God in Christ, reconciling the world to himself (2 Cor. V), saving his people by granting salvation to soul and body, and blessing his inheritance by freeing the nations from subjection to demons, so that the Son of God, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, may shepherd and lift them up forever and ever, reigning through all ages of ages. Amen.

## PSALM XXVIII

### A Psalm of David at the completion of the tabernacle

Bring to the Lord, sons of God; bring to the Lord the sons of rams. Bring to the Lord glory and honor; bring to the Lord glory for his name; worship the Lord in his holy court.

The voice of the Lord is over the waters. The God of majesty has thundered; the Lord is over many waters. The voice of the Lord is in power; the voice of the Lord is in magnificence.

The voice of the Lord breaks cedars, and the Lord will break the cedars of Lebanon. He will shatter them like a calf of Lebanon, and the Beloved like the son of unicorns. The voice of the Lord cuts through the flame of fire. The voice of the Lord shakes the desert, and the Lord will shake the desert of Kadesh.

The voice of the Lord prepares the hinds and reveals the dense places; and in his temple all will say, “Glory!” The Lord makes the flood dwell there, and the Lord will sit as King forever. The Lord will give strength to his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace.

## COMMENTARY

[Col. 0361B]

The title mentions the completion of the tabernacle. The completion of the tabernacle is the end of the world, in which the sons of God offer to God the sons of rams. The sons of rams are the lambs who are placed at the right hand, so that, offering glory and honor to his name in the pious works they have performed, they may worship the Lord—not now in buildings made by human hands, but in his holy court, that is, in Christ Jesus, in whom the fullness of divinity dwells (Col. II, 9).

“The voice of the Lord is over the waters.” When Jesus was baptized, with the heavens opened and the Holy Spirit coming in the form of a dove, the voice of the Lord came over the waters, saying: “You are my Son” (Matt. III).

“The God of majesty has thundered”—that is, he gave a voice over the waters, that is, over the sects of the nations, so that they might be brought to an end in the power and magnificence of Christ Jesus.

But whoever is rebellious and rises up like a cedar of Lebanon will be broken and shattered like the cedar of Lebanon. In Lebanon, even to this day, those who sacrifice to the most shameful Venus cut off the male organs of calves and place such things beneath them as offerings burned in her sacrifice; they offer to their goddess, the prostitute, the reward that their error deserved.

Thus those who have despised the chastity of Christ will be shattered like the calf of Lebanon, and they will be like the Beloved, the son of unicorns. Those will be pleased by the voice that cuts through the flame of fire—that is, those who are pleased by the voice that confers the grace of baptism, which began with the shaking of the wilderness.

For in the desert the Son of God blessed the streams of the Jordan and shook the desert of the very small town situated on the border of the wilderness, which is called Kadesh. There the voice of the Lord prepared hinds that would hasten to the springs of water [Col. 0361D], where he revealed what had been hidden—that is, concealed—so that, once these things had been revealed, all to whom they had been revealed might say glory in the temple of God and confess that the Lord dwells in the flood, in the water that washes away sins.

In that same flood the King will sit forever. There he will give strength to his people—to his people, I say, who believe in him. There he will bless his people with peace, he who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXIX

### A Psalm of song at the dedication of the house of David

I will exalt you, Lord, because you have received me and have not allowed my enemies to rejoice over me. Lord my God, I cried to you, and you healed me. Lord, you led my soul up from the underworld; you saved me from those descending into the pit.

Sing psalms to the Lord, his holy ones, and confess the memory of his holiness. For there is anger in his indignation, and life in his will. In the evening weeping will remain, but in the morning there will be joy.

But I said in my abundance, “I shall not be moved forever.” Lord, in your will you granted strength to my beauty. You turned your face away from me, and I became troubled.

To you, Lord, I will cry, and to my God I will plead: “What profit is there in my blood when I descend into corruption? Will dust confess to you, or will it announce your truth?”

The Lord heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper. You turned my mourning into joy for me; you tore off my sackcloth and surrounded me with gladness. So that my glory may sing to you and not be pierced with sorrow, Lord my God, I will confess to you forever.

## COMMENTARY

In the twenty-ninth psalm, the house of David is dedicated. That house is the one from David’s seed according to the flesh (Rom. I), not made by human hands but commanded by the word of the angel and constructed by the Holy Spirit.

It is that house which says to God: “I will exalt you, Lord, because you have received me.” For he received the form of a servant so that the enemies of the human race might not rejoice.

When Christ Jesus the Nazarene had been drawn out from the underworld and saved from those descending into the pit, all his apostles sing psalms to him and confess the memory of his holiness: for there was anger in his indignation when the world was cursed in the death of Adam, but now there is life in his will, as the Lord rises again [Col. 0362C].

“In the evening there will be weeping.” At the setting of all believers, there must necessarily be weeping because we are desolated by those who precede us, but in the morning we shall have joy with them.

At the first resurrection, as soon as the darkness of this world has ended and the morning time of resurrection has arrived, the beauty of our faith stands firm. Yet in his will the Lord grants strength to our beauty.

For if he turns his face away, however much we may love the Lord, we shall not love him more than Peter did. And if we say to him with Peter, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you” (Matt. XXVI), the treachery of denying him may befall us if he turns away from us.

Finally, it says: “Jesus turned and looked upon Peter as he was denying him,” and he also remembered that he had predicted this very thing to him. Peter went outside and wept most bitterly.

When the Lord therefore turned away from the one who presumed and said, “I shall not be moved forever,” he denied him; when he looked upon the denier, Peter wept, and the tears of the penitent washed away the guilt incurred by the presumptuous man.

For dust does not confess the Lord if it presumes, nor does it announce his truth if it boasts. But if, after sinning, it repents and displays its repentance through tears of love, it can say with Peter: “The Lord heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper.”

For he turned his mourning into joy, so that the one who had denied him three times might confess him three times. Yet this is only if the glory of the believer is exalted in God, not in human beings. Then he confidently says: “Lord my God, I will confess to you forever” [Col. 0363A], who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXX

### A Psalm of David. For the end, concerning ecstasy

In you, Lord, I have hoped; I shall not be confounded forever. In your righteousness deliver me; incline your ear to me; hasten to rescue me. Be for me a protecting God and a house of refuge, so that you may save me.

For you are my strength and my refuge, and for your name’s sake you will lead me and nourish me. You will bring me out of the snare that they have hidden for me, because you are my protector.

Into your hands I commend my spirit; you have redeemed me, Lord God of truth. You have hated those who observe vanities in vain. But I have hoped in the Lord; I will exult and rejoice in your mercy, because you have regarded my humiliation and saved my soul from distresses.

You have not shut me up in the hands of the enemy; you have set my feet in a spacious place. Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am afflicted. My eye, my soul, and my belly have been troubled in anger.

For my life has failed in sorrow and my years in groaning. My strength has weakened in poverty, and my bones have been troubled. I have become, beyond all my enemies, an object of great reproach to my neighbors, and a fear to my acquaintances.

Those who saw me fled from me. I have been forgotten like one dead, away from the heart. I have become like a ruined vessel, because I heard the reproach of many who dwell around me. While they gathered together against me to take my life, they conspired together [Col. 0363C].

But I have hoped in you, Lord. I said: “You are my God; my lots are in your hands.” Deliver me from the hands of my enemies and from those who persecute me. Make your face shine upon your servant; save me in your mercy, Lord. I shall not be confounded, because I have called upon you.

Let the impious be put to shame and led down into the underworld; let deceitful lips become mute, which speak iniquity against the righteous in pride and abuse.

How great is the abundance of your sweetness, Lord, which you have hidden for those who fear you! You have perfected it for those who hope in you, in the presence of the sons of men. You will hide them in the hiding-place of your face, from the disturbance of men. You will protect them in your tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues.

Blessed is the Lord, for he has made his mercy wondrous toward me in a fortified city. But I said in the excess of my mind: “I have been cast away from the sight of your eyes.” Therefore you heard the voice of my prayer when I cried to you.

Love the Lord, all his holy ones, for the Lord will seek out truth and repay abundantly those who act proudly. Act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all you who hope in the Lord.

## COMMENTARY
The thirtieth Psalm asserts that the hope which is in God delivers a person from eternal shame. For God, on account of his justice, liberates and rescues those who hope in him. He inclines his ear to them and hastens to rescue them, so that he may be their protecting God, like a house of refuge, that they may be saved; he rescues them from the snare that the demons secretly lay for them.

[Col. 0364A] If, nevertheless, he always says to the Lord, “Into your hands, Lord, I commend my spirit”—that is, “I commend my inner person into your hands”—then he does not make himself heed the vanity of this age, nor does he make himself rejoice in worldly things, but in your mercy, by which you have saved my soul from its necessities. When you looked upon my humiliation and did not shut me up in the hands of my enemy, but, taking me out of the narrow place where I was confined, set my feet in a spacious place.

But if you wish to make God merciful toward you, show yourself to be afflicted. For no one asks for mercy except the afflicted person, whose weeping disturbs his appearance; his soul and his belly, chastened by fasts, must remember this. For however long a person may live, his life fails amid sorrows; and however many years he may flourish, [Col. 0364B] his years fail amid groaning; and however much strength he may possess, his strength grows poor; and however confidently he may rely on bodily solidity, he will say, “My bones are troubled.”

This, certainly, must be guarded against: that he should become a reproach before all his enemies. If this condition befalls a righteous person, it makes him a martyr; if an unrighteous person, it sentences him to eternal death. For every saint has been hated unjustly, and the Lord himself also. Then the Holy Spirit cries out, as was foretold concerning Christ, so that the deceitful lips that speak iniquity against the righteous in arrogance and contempt may be silenced. And although the righteous suffer bitterness in this age, a great abundance of sweetness awaits them in the future, if they persevere; meanwhile, the Lord has hidden it from those who fear him.

He does not wish to reveal it in this age, [Col. 0364C] so that he may perfect it for those who hope in him before the sons of men who mocked them. And now indeed he hides them in the hiding-place of his face, so that, just as his own face was hidden—so hidden that he was thought to be merely a man—so also he hides these men, although they are great and holy, in the hiding-place of his face, away from human disturbance. Otherwise, once it had been revealed that they were holy and friends of God, their purpose might be disturbed by human flattery.

But then he makes his mercy marvelous in them, when the city of those who surround it appears—the city surrounded by angels, the mother-city of the saints, Jerusalem. What will the righteous person say there? “When I saw myself in this age regarded by everyone as dung, I said in my heart, ‘I have been cast away from the sight of your eyes.’ But you heard the voice, because I cried out to you.” [Col. 0364D]

Therefore, saints of the Lord, do not be afraid if human arrogance oppresses you. For there will be a judgment in which the Lord will seek out the truth and repay those who practice arrogance abundantly. Act manfully now; do not fail, but let your heart be strengthened. Be confident, all you who hope in the Lord, who lives and reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXXI

**A Psalm of David; for understanding.**

Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not imputed sin, and in whose spirit there is no deceit. For while I was silent, my bones grew old, while I cried out [Col. 0365A] all day. For day and night your hand was heavy upon me; I was turned into misery, while the thorn was being fixed. I made my sin known to you, and I did not hide my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my iniquity against myself to the Lord”; and you forgave the wickedness of my sin. For this every holy person will pray to you at an opportune time. Nevertheless, in a flood of many waters they will not come near him. You are my refuge from the tribulation that surrounded me; my rejoicing, rescue me from those who surround me. I will give you understanding and instruct you in this way in which you will walk; I will fix my eyes upon you. Do not become like a horse or a mule, in which there is no understanding. With bit and bridle bind their jaws, for they do not come near you. Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy will surround the one who hopes in the Lord. [Col. 0365B] Rejoice in the Lord and exult, righteous ones, and glory, all you upright of heart.

## Commentary

This thirty-first Psalm has placed its title under the heading of understanding, so that it may give understanding, instruct the believer in the way in which he walks, and fix its eyes upon him, lest he become like a horse or a mule, in which there is no understanding.

Let us nevertheless attend to the beginning of the Psalm, in which those are declared blessed whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered. For unless someone has been reborn of water and the Holy Spirit (John 3), this cannot happen to him. But who is this one who forgives sins? Without doubt, he of whom it is said, “He committed no deceit in his mouth” (1 Peter 2). [Col. 0365C]

Thus the whole world, set amid a bramble and placed in a wound—for the hand of God was heavy upon it and it had been turned into misery because its spine had been broken, the spine that raised up the freedom of its neck and head—continually cried out through the voices of the prophets, so that the one who would save it might come. But when the Lord came, it became silent: “while I cried out.” For when the Lord came, the Law and the Prophets, who were crying out, became silent. And while each one pronounced judgment against him on account of his own sin, he forgives the wickedness of his heart, for which every holy person prays at the opportune time.

We give the saints an opportune time to pray for our sins when we turn away from sin. For when he says, “In a flood of many waters [Col. 0365D] they will not come near him,” he shows that through the one water of baptism people draw near to God. This water is a refuge from the oppression of the demons that surround us. He also gives us understanding and will thus instruct us in the way in which we shall enter, so that he may fix his eyes upon us, lest we become like a horse or a mule.

Those who do not wish to draw near will be restrained by the bridle of tribulation and the bit of judgment placed upon their jaws, because they do not draw near to him. For the scourges of sinners are many; but those who hope in the Lord will be surrounded by the Lord’s mercy. But you who come to the Lord not by bit and bridle, but by the judgment of a good will, rejoice in the Lord and exult, righteous ones, and glory, all you upright of heart, in Christ Jesus our Lord, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

[Col. 0366A]

## PSALM XXXII

**A Psalm of David; for the end.**

Rejoice in the Lord, righteous ones; praise is fitting for the upright. Give thanks to the Lord on the lyre; sing psalms to him on the ten-stringed psaltery. Sing to him a new song; sing well to him with a shout. For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his works are in faithfulness. He loves mercy and judgment; the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.

By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth all their power. Gathering the waters of the sea as in a wineskin, putting the abysses into storehouses. Let all the earth fear the Lord, and let all who inhabit the world be moved by him. For he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created.

The Lord scatters the counsels [Col. 0366B] of the nations; he rejects the thoughts of the peoples, and he rejects the plans of rulers. But the counsel of the Lord remains forever; the thoughts of his heart remain from generation to generation. Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom he chose as his inheritance.

From heaven the Lord looked down; he saw all the sons of men. From his prepared dwelling-place he looked upon all who inhabit the earth. He formed their hearts individually; he understands all their works. A king is not saved by great strength, nor will a giant be saved by the abundance of his power. A horse is deceptive for salvation; in the abundance of its strength it will be saved.

Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him and upon those who hope in his mercy, to rescue their souls from death and nourish [Col. 0366C] them in famine. Our soul patiently awaits the Lord, for he is our helper and protector. For in him our heart will rejoice, and in his holy name we will hope. Let your mercy, Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in you.

## Commentary

If, from the beginning of the age, the righteous of God have suffered afflictions and tribulations in this world, how is it said, “Rejoice, righteous ones”? Does he call one who is being scourged and afflicted by various kinds of tortures to rejoice? Whoever says this should consider the Apostle, who teaches us not only to rejoice in these things but even to take pleasure in persecutions. Hence the apostle James says, “Consider it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various trials” (James 1:2).

But the master of the apostles [Col. 0366D] teaches how we should rejoice: “When people persecute you,” he says, “and falsely say every evil thing against you, rejoice and exult, because your reward is great in heaven” (Matthew 5). If you are upright in faith, do not seek human praises on earth, because you will have those of the angels in heaven. There praise is fitting for you, where your praise will have no end at all.

Now give thanks to the Lord on the lyre, and let that lyre have ten strings, recalling the virtues of the Decalogue and imposing the observance of the commandments.

The first string sounds the Lord’s upright, orthodox word, and all his works in faith. The second string sounds because he loves mercy and judgment. The third string should sound because the mercy of the Lord fills the earth to such an extent that, on account of the whole human race, the Son of God was crucified. The fourth string [Col. 0367A] should sound because the heavens were established by words—that is, the apostles were strengthened.

Anyone who wishes to be properly instructed about these heavens will be taught by reading Genesis. Here he is speaking of those heavens that proclaim the glory of God rising from the dead and ascending into the heavens. The fifth string followed: the breath of the mouth of our Lord Jesus Christ is all their power.

Let the sixth now speak: that the waters of the sea are gathered as in a wineskin and the abyss is placed in God’s storehouses. What is the abyss in God’s storehouse? And what is the abyss in which the punishments of the demons dwell? Carefully observe: the one who was saying, “O the depth of the riches of the wisdom of God!” (Romans 11), found the abyss in God’s storehouse. Therefore, when you seek the hidden things of God’s knowledge with a pure heart and upright faith, know that you are striking the sixth string.

There is another abyss where demons dwell: the investigation of heretics. Concerning this the Apostle cries out to us, “Do not be high-minded, but fear” (Romans 11). As for the waters of the sea being gathered, the sects of all nations have been collected at one fountain of living water, so that from this one wineskin they may receive water springing up to eternal life.

Therefore the seventh string sounds this: “Let all the earth fear the Lord”—not Judea alone, but all who inhabit the world. The eighth signifies that our Lord Jesus Christ himself is the creator of all things. He scattered the counsels of the nations in idols; he rejected the thoughts of the peoples in the synagogues; he rejects the plans of rulers through the sufferings of martyrs; and he makes the counsel of the Lord remain forever in the churches, in which are the thoughts of his heart, [Col. 0367C] forever and ever.

The ninth string indicates that blessed is the nation that knows the Lord Jesus Christ as its God, and that this is the people whom he chose as his inheritance. The tenth string indicates that the Lord looked down upon us from heaven—not from heaven as though through a window, but from his prepared dwelling-place, that is, from the perfect man whom he assumed.

From this one, therefore, whom the Virgin bore, he looked upon everyone without respect of persons. For he was both born and suffered for all—the very one who formed their hearts individually. He did not need anyone to bear witness to him concerning humanity. He saw what was taking place in a person so clearly that he could bring forth into the open what each person was thinking.

As for the statement that a king is not saved by great strength, it means the same as if one were to say to Herod: [Col. 0367D] “What? Because you are powerful, are you able to persecute Christ so thoroughly that you can examine the scribes, interrogate the magi, and kill infants? In the abundance of your strength you will not be saved, just as the one who trusted in his horse was not saved, and of whom it is sung, ‘He cast horse and rider into the sea’ (Exodus 15).”

The horse deceived him for salvation; so too, even if you are a giant in your strength, you will not be saved. For the eyes of the Lord do not look upon those who trust in their own strength, but upon those who hope in his mercy. He rescues their souls from death and nourishes them in famine.

If they suffer hunger in this age and say with the Apostle, “To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty and naked” (1 Corinthians 4), they nevertheless add, saying, “Our soul acts patiently; it is not disturbed, awaiting the Lord.” [Col. 0368A] For he is our helper and protector. And just as we were commanded at the head of the Psalm, “Rejoice, righteous ones, in the Lord,” so our heart will rejoice in him, and we have hoped in his holy name. He himself shows mercy to us, as we have hoped in him, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXXIII

**A Psalm of David, when he changed his appearance before Abimelech, dismissed him, and departed.**

I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth. In the Lord my soul will be praised; let the meek hear and rejoice. Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together. I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and he delivered me from all my tribulations. [Col. 0368B] Draw near to him and be enlightened, and your faces will not be put to shame.

This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him and saved him from all his tribulations. The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and he will rescue them. Taste and see that the Lord is sweet. Blessed is the man who hopes in him.

Fear the Lord, all you his saints, for there is no lack for those who fear him. The rich have been in need and have been hungry, but those who seek the Lord will not be deprived of any good. Come, children; hear me. I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the person who desires life and loves to see good days? Restrain your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit. Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are toward their prayers. But the face of the Lord is against those who do [Col. 0368C] evil, to destroy their memory from the earth. The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them and delivered them from all their tribulations. The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit.

Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord delivered them from all of them. The Lord guards all their bones; not one of them will be broken. The death of sinners is most grievous, and those who hate the righteous will go astray. The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and all who hope in him will not go astray.

## Commentary

Unless you change your appearance before the prince of vices, dismiss him, and devote to the Lord of virtues whatever time of life remains to you, you are not [Col. 0368D] truly saying, “I will bless the Lord at all times.” Nor will the praise of God always be in your mouth if the vice of cursing and bitterness is alive in you.

Let the praise of God therefore be in your mouth. Do not become accustomed to flattering human beings with praises, and do not fear that those whom you justly rebuke will unjustly revile you. For if you are reviled by a human being, you will be praised by God. If you have saddened the arrogant, let the meek hear and rejoice—those who magnify the Lord with you and exalt his name together.

Let us now examine the reasons for his praise: “I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and he delivered me from all my afflictions.” And you too, he says, who are blind in heart, draw near to him; draw near and be enlightened, and your faces will not be put to shame.

Your faces will not be ashamed in poverty [Col. 0369A] if you consider that he is Lord of all things, rich in heaven and earth, who became poor for our poverty and was afflicted for our affliction. You will neither blush in poverty nor fail in tribulation.

For this poor man cried out on the cross. Who is the poor man? The one who, in order to make you rich, became poor. He became obedient unto the cross (Philippians 2), in order to free you from torments. He cried out, and the Lord heard him; he sent his angel around those who fear his body, rolled away the stone from the tomb (Matthew 28), and rescued him.

Taste the body of life and see how sweet the Lord is. For he has life in himself; whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has life (John 6). Then blessed will be the person who hopes in him.

Fear the Lord, all you his saints, for those who fear him lack nothing. Nothing is lacking in the present from virtues; nothing is lacking for perfection, so that nothing will be lacking from joys in the future.

For the riches of the present age usually abandon their lovers so completely that you may see those who were rich and whose arrogance no one could bear become needy and hungry. Therefore the riches bestowed by the world are placed in uncertainty. But the riches that the Lord bestows will not fail; they remain in every good, and because these riches arise from the fear of God, he says: “Fear the Lord, his saints, because those who fear him lack nothing.”

You who desire to be eternally rich, come to me as children to a father. The Holy Spirit cries out, “Come and hear me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.” He wishes to be taught the fear of the Lord who desires eternal life and wants to see good days.

You fear the Lord, therefore, not if you fear him as one who thunders, flashes lightning, or causes an earthquake, but if you dread him as one who threatens eternal fire. For just as the person who restrains his tongue from evil possesses life, and just as the ears of the Lord are toward the prayer of the one who turns away from evil in order to do good, so the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy their memory from the earth.

It should certainly be noted that, among the other marks of virtue, peace also is commanded to be sought: “Seek peace,” he says, “and pursue it.” For peace gives people good days in the present, and in the future grants them the dignity of the children of God, according to what the Lord himself says: “Blessed are the peacemakers, because they will be called sons of God” (Matthew 5).

Nor should what we see in this age frighten us: that the righteous have many tribulations. [Col. 0369D] These tribulations pass away, and the Lord delivers them from all of them. He also guards all their bones in the tomb and preserves them for the resurrection, so that not one of them will suffer destruction on the day of resurrection.

But the death of sinners will appear most grievous at the time when he raises the souls of his own in their bodies. Know this, he says: everyone who hopes in him does not sin. At the end of the Psalm he commends abstinence from sins to those who hope in the Lord, so that they may reach the fruit of their hope: “For not all who hope in him sin,” he says.

But in order that we may not sin, we must earnestly ask the mercy of the one who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

[Col. 0370A]

## PSALM XXXIV

**A Psalm of David; for the end.**

Judge, Lord, those who harm me; fight against those who fight me. Take up arms and shield, and rise to help me. Draw the sword and close the way against those who persecute me; say to my soul, “I am your salvation.” Let those who seek my soul be confounded and put to shame. Let those who think evil against me be turned backward and confounded.

Let them become like dust before the face of the wind, and let the angel of the Lord hem them in. Let their way be darkness and slippery ground, and let the angel of the Lord pursue them. For without cause they secretly hid the destruction of their snare [Col. 0370B] for me; needlessly they reproached my soul.

Let the snare he does not know come upon him, and let the trap he hid seize him; let him fall into that very snare. But my soul will exult in the Lord and rejoice over his salvation. All my bones will say, “Lord, who is like you?” You will rescue the poor from the hand of one stronger than he, the needy and the poor from those who plunder him.

Unjust witnesses rose up; they questioned me about things I did not know. They repaid me evil for good, barrenness for my soul. But when they troubled me, I clothed myself in sackcloth; I humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer returned to my bosom.

As though he were my neighbor and our brother, so I was pleased with him; as one mourning and sorrowful, so I humbled myself. And they rejoiced against me and gathered together; scourges were gathered against me, and I did not know it. They were scattered, but they were not pierced with remorse; they tested me, mocked me with mockery, and gnashed [Col. 0370C] their teeth against me.

Lord, when will you look upon this? Restore my soul from their wickedness, my only one from lions. I will give thanks to you in the great Church; in a weighty people I will praise you.

Let those who unjustly oppose me not rejoice over me; those who hate me without cause and wink with their eyes. For they spoke peacefully to me, but in the anger of the earth, while speaking, they devised deceits. They opened their mouths wide against me and said, “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it.”

You have seen, Lord; do not be silent. Lord, do not depart from me. Rise and attend to my judgment, my God and my Lord, to my cause. Judge me according to your justice, Lord my God, and let them not rejoice over me.

Let them not say in their hearts, “Aha, aha, our soul!” Nor let them say, “We have devoured him.” Let those who rejoice in my evils be confounded and put to shame together. Let those [Col. 0370D] who speak evil against me be clothed with shame and reverence.

Let those who desire my justice exult and rejoice, and let them always say, “The Lord is magnified, who desires the peace of his servant.” And my tongue will meditate on your justice; all day long, on your praise.

## Commentary

If the Lord Jesus Christ had seen that the Scriptures of the Old Testament were contrary to his commandments, he would have excluded them from his Church. But now, since he not only did not exclude them, but also asserted that they had been sanctified by the Father—for when he gave testimony concerning the sons of God and spoke the verse of the eighty-first Psalm, he said, “Scripture cannot be changed: [him] whom the Father sanctified and sent into this world” (John 10)—what shall we do?

If we curse our enemies, we despise the evangelical commandments, by which we are ordered not only not to curse them but even to pray for them. If we wish to keep the commands of the Gospel, we abandon the Psalms, in which enemies are frequently cursed, as in this passage at the beginning [Col. 0371A] of the Psalm: “Judge,” he says, “those who harm me,” and the rest that follows.

Therefore the Psalmist gives the more cautious instruction: Take care not to think that these words apply to human beings who oppose you. Rather, standing firm in faith, pray for your enemies as you have been commanded, and understand this prayer of the present Psalm to be directed not against flesh and blood but against the spirits of this air, who harm us daily and wage war daily.

Put on sackcloth, or a haircloth, and humble your soul through fasting, because they are conquered only through prayer and fasting. Why do you pray clothed in sackcloth? So that the Lord may defeat those who fight against you, and take up the weapons of his help— invisible [Col. 0371B] weapons against invisible enemies.

For they seek your soul. Pray that their way may become darkness and slippery ground, and that the angel of the Lord may pursue those who secretly hid their snare of destruction for you, reproaching your soul as worthless and saying to it, “It is useless that you pray, that you fast, that you despise the world.”

Hence the prophet rebukes this very thing, saying, “Therefore,” he says, “the plague upon Israel has been multiplied, because they said, ‘He who fears God is useless.’”

Since these unclean spirits, by their suggestions, reproach my soul as worthless, so that, considering itself insignificant, it may withdraw from the precious fear of God, [Col. 0371C] let the snare they do not know come upon them. Just as the invisible enemies are against me as I advance toward the good, so let an invisible snare confront them as they hurry toward my destruction. Let the trap they had concealed for me seize them, and let them fall into that same snare, so that my soul may exult in God my Savior, who rescues the poor from the hand of one stronger than he.

In this, unjust witnesses rise up, showing what is beautiful to be foul and what is hostile to be good. They questioned me about things I did not know and that I did not have at all in my soul; they repaid me evil for good.

The demons’ repayment of evil for good is such that I might say, “As often as I pray, as often as I abstain from sins, evil things happen to me, and barrenness accompanies my soul.” What did you do, then, when they troubled you? Tell us, so that we may immediately do the same.

“When many troubled me,” he says, “I clothed myself in sackcloth, humbled my soul through fasting, and my prayer was turned back into my bosom.”

Whoever I regarded as a neighbor and as a brother, and whom I considered faithful and took pleasure in, acted toward me as Judas acted toward the Lord: he made me mourning and sorrowful, and humbled me before my enemies.

You may apply this to the Lord’s Passion, while nevertheless maintaining the order of the explanation already begun, because the Lord’s Passion itself works for our edification. For the more closely you cling to God, the more numerous will be the scourges of demons around you. They test you, mock you with their laughter, and gnash [Col. 0371D] their teeth against you.

Cry out what belongs to you: “Lord, when will you look upon this? Restore my soul from their evil deeds, my only one from lions.” [Col. 0372A] Our soul is one, both in number and in affection. Therefore, when you restore it to a good purpose and free it from their evil deeds, then I will give thanks to you in the great Church and among a people that is not frivolous, does not pursue spectacles, and does not show favoritism, but is a weighty people that guards the fear of you.

I will have continual fellowship among this people, and among the same people I will praise you. Therefore, let the wicked who oppose me not insult me—those who hate me without cause and wink with their eyes.

As I said, apply these things to the Lord’s Passion in such a way that you do not altogether omit their interpretation for your edification. For the demons speak peacefully to us every day. The fruit of desire is a peaceful thing; but beneath anger they devise deceits. It is like bait on a hook: sweet to look at, deadly [Col. 0372B] to taste.

They opened their mouths wide against me. Every day lovers of the world commit unheard-of crimes, and no one at all rebukes anyone. But if someone of good purpose falls into some slight fault, the unclean spirits open their mouths wide against him—those who, as I said, devote themselves to crimes—so that you see them pass such judgment on a minor sin that they say, “Why are they not driven from the city? Why are they permitted to live? These are the people through whom the world perished.”

Here he cries out to the Lord: “Rise, Lord, and attend to my judgment; judge my cause according to your mercy.” For if you judge according to your mercy, the demons will not insult me, nor will they say, “Aha, aha, my soul!” Nor will they say, “We have devoured him.”

“Aha, aha” is understood both in a good sense and in an evil one. For it is said, “Well done, good and faithful servant” (Matthew 25; Luke 19), and it is also said, “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it.” Thus “aha” is the cry of one whose desire appears to have been fulfilled, whether for good or for evil. [Col. 0372C]

Therefore, as soon as those who rejoice in your evil cease saying, “We have devoured him,” let those who rejoice in your evils be confounded. Let those who desire your justice and long for your peace rejoice, so that your tongue may meditate on God’s justice and you may remain every day in his praise, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXXV

**A discourse of the Lord; of David; for the end.**

The unrighteous person said within himself that he would sin; there is no fear of God before his eyes. For he acted deceitfully in [Col. 0372D] his own sight, so that his iniquity might be found hateful. The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit; he did not wish to understand, so as to do good. He meditated on iniquity in his bed; he stood upon every evil way, but he did not hate wickedness.

Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your truth reaches to the clouds. Your justice is like the mountains of God; your judgments are a great abyss. You will save human beings and beasts, Lord, as you have multiplied your mercy, O God.

But the sons of men will hope in the shelter of your wings. They will be intoxicated by the abundance of your house, and you will give them drink from the torrent of your delight. For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light.

Extend your mercy to those who know you, and your justice to those who are upright of heart. Let not the foot of arrogance come upon me, and let not the hand of the sinner move me. [Col. 0373A] There the workers of iniquity have fallen; they have been driven out and could not stand.

## Commentary

A distinction must be made between the one who sins against another and the one who sins against himself. He sins against another who, although he is able to correct a person who is sinning from evil, instead flatters him. He sins against himself who does not wish to persuade himself to practice justice, because there is no fear of God in his sight, so that his iniquity may be found hateful. He praises the unjust person so that the unjust person may be praised. He does not wish to understand the good actions by which he may make God the dwelling-place of his heart.

He meditates on iniquity so that he may stand upon every evil way and not loathe wickedness. Although the Lord’s mercy is on land and sea, it is especially [Col. 0373B] in heaven; from there it comes, and from there it is awaited.

His truth reaches to the apostles, who are called clouds because, by the downpour of their preaching, they watered the earth of faith and taught it to bear fruit for God. Hence the Lord says concerning them, “I will command the clouds not to rain rain upon Judea” (Isaiah 5:6).

His truth reaches to them—the truth who is Christ—whose justice is like the mountains of God and whose judgments are a great abyss. By his coming he will save both human beings and beasts, that is, Jews and Gentiles.

The sons of men, who had become despairing while remaining in Adam’s sin, hope in the protection of his wings, that is, in the outspread hands fixed [Col. 0373C] upon the cross. They hope who are intoxicated by the abundance of his house. His house is the one that flowed from his side; from it those who believe are intoxicated. He will give drink from the torrent of his delights to those who have been intoxicated by the abundance of his house.

For with him is the fountain of life. Since he is light from light, in his light we shall see light. He extends his mercy to those who know him, and his justice to those who are upright of heart. He both extends forgiveness to the one who corrects and preserves justice for the one who persists. [Col. 0373D]

Therefore we must pray that the foot of arrogance may not come upon us and that the hand of the sinner may not move us. For all who work iniquity are in the hand of the devil; having despaired of God’s mercy, they have been driven out and could not stand.

But the Apostle says, “He will stand; God is able to make him stand” (Romans 14). Therefore the Lord Jesus Christ must be entreated to strengthen us himself, so that we may be able to stand in his fear, through our Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns in the unity of the Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XXXVI

**A Psalm of David himself.**
Do not emulate those who do evil, nor envy those who commit iniquity. For they will wither quickly like grass, and fade like the green plants.
