Hope in the Lord, do good, dwell in the land, and you will be nourished by its riches. Delight in the Lord, and he will grant you the requests of your heart. Commit your way to the Lord, hope in him, and he will act. He will bring forth your righteousness like the light, and your judgment like [Col. 0374A] noonday. Submit yourself to the Lord and pray to him. Do not envy one who prospers in his way, a man who commits injustices. Cease from anger and abandon wrath; do not envy others in order to do evil. For those who do evil will be destroyed, but those who wait for the Lord will inherit the land.

And yet a little while, and the sinner will be no more; you will seek his place, and will not find it. But the meek will inherit the land and delight in an abundance of peace. The sinner watches the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him. But the Lord will laugh at him, because he sees that his day is coming. Sinners have drawn the sword; they have bent their bow, to deceive the poor and needy, to slaughter those who are upright in heart. Let their sword enter their own hearts, and let their bows be broken.

Better is the little [Col. 0374B] possessed by the righteous than the great riches of sinners. For the arms of sinners will be broken, but the Lord strengthens the righteous. The Lord knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance will be forever. They will not be put to shame in an evil time, and in days of famine they will be satisfied, because sinners will perish. But the enemies of the Lord, as soon as they have been honored and exalted, will fail; like smoke, they will fail away.

The sinner borrows and does not repay, but the righteous person has compassion and gives in return. For those who bless him will inherit the land, but those who curse him will perish. The steps of a man are directed by the Lord, and he delights in his way. When he falls, he will not be crushed, because the Lord supports him with his hand.

I was young, and now I am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his offspring seeking bread. All day long he shows mercy and [Col. 0374C] lends, and his offspring will be in blessing. Turn away from evil and do good; dwell forever and ever. For the Lord loves judgment and will not forsake his holy ones; they will be preserved forever. The unjust will be punished, and the offspring of the ungodly will perish.

But the righteous will inherit the land and dwell upon it forever and ever. The mouth of the righteous will meditate on wisdom, and his tongue will speak judgment. The law of his God is in his heart, and his steps will not be overthrown. The sinner watches the righteous and seeks to put him to death. But the Lord will not abandon him into his hands, nor condemn him when judgment is passed upon him.

Wait for the Lord and keep his way, and he will exalt you so that you may inherit the land; when sinners have perished, you will see it. I saw the impious man exalted and raised up like the cedars of Lebanon. I passed by, and behold, [Col. 0374D] he was not there; I sought him, and his place was not found.

Keep innocence and observe equity, for there are remnants for the peaceful man. But the unjust will perish; the remnants of the ungodly will perish together. The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, and he is their protector in the time of tribulation. The Lord will help them and deliver them; he will rescue and save them from sinners, because they have hoped in him.

## Commentary

If this hope, which is seen, is sought, we will envy those who do evil and those who commit iniquity. For we can say: “Look, that man and that man have perpetrated such crimes, and yet they flourish.” “Do not consider this,” he says, “but consider [Col. 0375A] that they will wither quickly like grass.” You, however, hope in God and do good; hope, because “we have been saved by hope” (Romans 8:24). “Dwell in the land and be nourished by its riches.” Dwell in the land—that is, in your body—and you will be nourished by its riches. If you work your land, you will be filled with bread.

Let the eyes offer fruit from heavenly desire; let the ears offer attentiveness for hearing the word of God; let the mouth be occupied with divine praises; the hands, with almsgiving; the belly, with fasts; and let the whole body be occupied with the virtues of chastity. Thus, dwelling in the land, you will be nourished by its riches. Then you will delight in the Lord, and he will grant you the request of your heart.

When you have committed your way to him, he will bring forth your righteousness like the light and make your judgment bright like noonday. For nothing is brighter than noonday [Col. 0375B]. At that time the perfect light advances. “Submit yourself to the Lord and pray to him,” as though he were saying: If you have not submitted yourself to him in order to do his will, you plead with him without cause.

Do not envy the man who prospers, the man who commits iniquity. Cease from anger and abandon wrath. Do not envy others in order to do evil, because those who do evil will be destroyed. What is delayed is not taken away: “A little while, and the sinner will be no more. You will seek his place, and will not find it.”

For “the meek will possess the land” (Matthew 5:5)—not this land, the mother of thorns and serpents, but that land in which eternity reigns, the land flowing with milk and honey. There they will delight in an abundance of peace.

If you are righteous, take care not to seek these things in the present world. For you will not be better than Paul, who endured [Col. 0375C] hunger and thirst and persevered in cold and nakedness. But be vigilant, because the devil watches you every day and gnashes his teeth over you. Yet the Lord laughs at him, because he knows that his day is coming.

However many battles the demons may wage against you, do not be afraid, because their swords will enter their own hearts and their bows will be broken. It is better for you to possess a little righteousness than great riches acquired through injustice by sinners. For if you fight, the Lord will break the arms of the demons. He deigns to strengthen his righteous ones by his mercy, those whose blameless ways he knows and whose inheritance is Christ.

He who remains forever will not be put to shame through Christ in an evil time. The evil time for a Christian is when he is urged toward some [Col. 0375D] sin. But if his inheritance remains forever—that is, if he perseveres in Christ—he will not be put to shame in an evil time, and in days of famine he will be satisfied.

This is the time when sinners perish. At present, however, even the enemies of the Lord reign. Although they are honored and exalted by flatterers, they will fail; like smoke, they will immediately fail away. But the righteous will abound, give generously, and distribute. The unjust man, however, will even borrow and not repay. The greedy person is always in need.

But because the steps of the righteous are directed by the Lord, even if he falls he will not be crushed, because the Lord supports him with his hand. Recall the beginning, and you will see that the righteous person has been tested rather than deceived; he is not abandoned.

He who turns away from evil in order to do good will be preserved forever, [Col. 0376A] because his mouth will meditate on wisdom. For the law of God is in his heart, and therefore his steps will not be overthrown. The devil watches him and desires to put him to death, but God will not abandon him into his hands, nor condemn him when judgment is passed upon him.

Wait for the Lord and keep his ways, and he will exalt you so that you may inherit the land. When sinners perish, you will see it.

At this point, although our conscience reminds us that many men have suddenly fallen from power and have come to nothing, so that they have left behind not even the place of their journey, nevertheless he speaks here especially of the devil. For he is the impious one exalted above the cedars of Lebanon. But when the world has passed away, his place will be sought and will not be found.

Let us preserve the unity of faith, so that we may see the equity of judgment. He will leave remnants [Col. 0376B] for the peaceful man, but he will punish the unjust together. The remnants of the ungodly will perish when the salvation of the righteous comes from the Lord, and he becomes their protector in the time of tribulation.

But in order that they may escape, the Lord helps them, delivers them, rescues them from sinners, and saves them, because they hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

# PSALM XXXVII

*A psalm of David, for the remembrance of the Sabbath.*

O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, nor correct me in your wrath. For your arrows are fixed in me, and you have strengthened your hand against me. There is no health in my flesh because of your anger; there is no peace in my bones because of [Col. 0376C] my sins. For my iniquities have risen above my head, and like a heavy burden they have weighed heavily upon me. My wounds have festered and become corrupt because of my folly.

I have become miserable and have been bowed down completely; all day long I went about in sorrow. For my loins are filled with delusions, and there is no health in my flesh. I have been afflicted and humbled exceedingly; I roared because of the groaning of my heart.

O Lord, all my desire is before you, and my groaning is not hidden from you. My heart is troubled; my strength has abandoned me, and the light of my eyes—even that is not with me.

My friends and my neighbors approached and stood against me. Those who were near me stood far away, and those who sought my life used violence. Those who sought evil [Col. 0376D] against me spoke vanities and meditated on deceits all day long.

But I, like a deaf man, did not hear, and like a mute man who does not open his mouth. I became like a man who does not hear and who has no rebukes in his mouth. For in you, O Lord, I have hoped; you will hear me, O Lord my God.

For I said: “May my enemies never rejoice over me; and when my feet are shaken, may they not speak great things against me.” For I am ready for scourges, and my pain is always before me. For I will declare my iniquity, and I will think upon my sin.

But my enemies live, and they have grown strong against me; those who hate me unjustly have multiplied. Those who repay evil for good slandered me, because I followed goodness.

Do not abandon me, [Col. 0377A] O Lord my God; do not depart from me. Attend to my help, O Lord, my God of salvation.

## Commentary

Someone rightly wished to apply this psalm to the passion of blessed Job in an exposition of it. But anyone who desires to read and understand Job’s passion will do better to examine Job’s own book.

Here, however, the same penitent who appears in the sixth psalm cries out to the Lord not to be rebuked in the Lord’s anger, or for divine fury to rage in his correction. Certainly, whenever you read of such movements in God, he does not feel anger according to what you suffer, because God is impassible. He chastises not through agitation but through equity.

Nevertheless, when we feel anger, we call it fury, because we suffer a poverty both [Col. 0377B] of speech and of reason. Concerning the incorporeal, we speak in bodily terms; concerning the impassible, in terms of passion. We testify according to what we can say, not according to what he is.

Finally, it follows: “For your arrows are fixed in me.” Does the fact that he mentions arrows mean that they are real arrows? Indeed, they are the true arrows by which we are spiritually pierced, so that we may understand that there is no health in our flesh when we are driven by the wounds of lust. There is the wound of the Lord’s anger; there our bones have no peace because of our sins.

When our iniquities rise above our head—our head is Christ—our iniquities rise above our head whenever we do anything against his commands, and, like a heavy burden, they weigh upon us. Because we delay, they fester [Col. 0377C] in our wounds and make those wounds worse. Because of our folly we become miserable and are troubled completely.

Why, then, do we become sad in the very midst of sin? Because we recognize that our soul is filled with the delusions of demons, and therefore that there is no health in our flesh. Let us therefore be bowed down and humbled completely. Returning the groaning and lamentation of our heart, let us cry out from our inmost being: “O Lord, all my desire is before you.”

Even while placed in these sins, let us desire to be separated from sins. We are taught to pray that divine mercy may grant this desire, because our heart is troubled, our strength deserts us, and the light of our eyes—that is, Christ—and the Holy Spirit are not with us.

When we are occupied with pollutions, then our friends, the precepts [Col. 0377D] of God, come against us, stand before us, rebuke us, and threaten us with eternal fire and sudden death. But our neighbors stand far away—that is, the holy angels, who are near to us when we live justly, devoutly, and chastely.

Because they cannot be near pollution or impiety, they therefore stand far away. While they stand far away through our fault, those who seek our soul use violence against us; and, seeking our harm, they suggest vanity and meditate on deceits all day long.

But whoever wishes to reach mercy says what follows: “I, like a deaf man, did not hear.” When they provoked me to break out in some shameful or evil word, I became like a mute man who does not open his mouth. Why? Because I hope in you, O Lord. For by hope [Col. 0378A] we are saved, and we believe.

For you hear, O Lord God, so that our enemies may not insult us. Which enemies? Those who speak great things against us when our feet are shaken.

We say these things if we acknowledge that, because of our sins, we are ready for scourges, and if the pain of our heart acts against us and, by declaring our iniquity, makes us think upon our sin.

Our enemies live and are strengthened against us when we sin. But when we do not sin, they multiply in order to hate us unjustly and repay us with evil for good. Thus, while we pray and conduct ourselves chastely, they, moved by jealousy, repay our good with evil and cause us to be slandered when we follow righteousness.

Therefore we must cry out to the Lord. May he not abandon us because [Col. 0378B] of our sins, but attend to our help. In him we repent of the past; we correct the present; may he direct the future. Thus, as the title placed over the psalm proclaims the remembrance of the Sabbath, let us cease from every servile work, so that we may be freed from the slavery of sin, through our Lord Jesus Christ, who, in the unity of the Godhead, reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit before all things, and now and always, and throughout all ages. Amen.

# PSALM XXXVIII

*For the end; a song of David for Jeduthun.*

I said: “I will guard my ways, so that I do not sin with my tongue.” I set a guard over my mouth when the sinner stood against me. I was silent and humbled myself; I kept silence [Col. 0378C] even from good things, and my pain was renewed.

My heart grew hot within me, and in my meditation the fire burned. I spoke with my tongue: “Make known to me, O Lord, my end, and what the number of my days is, so that I may know what is lacking to me.”

Behold, you have made my days measurable, and my substance is as nothing before you. Yet every living man is altogether vanity. Yet man passes by like an image; indeed, he is troubled in vain. He stores up treasure and does not know for whom he will gather it.

And now what is my expectation? Is it not the Lord? And my substance is with you. Deliver me from all my iniquities; you have made me a reproach to the fool.

I was silent and did not open my mouth, because you have done this to me. Because of the strength of your hand I failed under rebukes; because of iniquity you corrected man. And you caused [Col. 0378D] his soul to waste away like a spider; yet every man is troubled in vain.

Hear my prayer, O Lord, and listen with your ears to my supplication and my tears. Do not be silent, for I am a sojourner with you and a stranger, like all my fathers. Forgive me, so that I may recover my breath before I depart and exist no longer.

## Commentary

In the thirty-eighth psalm we see the profession of a holy purpose begun. In it the things that the man of God said, thought, suffered, meditated upon, and prayed are explained.

Let us hear, then, what he said. Let us suppose that he had heard: “Run while you have the light, lest the darkness overtake you.” Wishing [Col. 0379A] to run, he said that he would guard his ways.

First of all, he acted so as not to sin with his tongue; he set a guard over his mouth. When? Did he remain silent always? Not at every time, but while the sinner stood against him—the sinner who provoked him either to curse, to revile, to slander, or even to bring forth some evil from his mouth.

At that time he became silent, humbled himself, and kept silence not only from evil things but also from good things. Paul acted more perfectly: he did not keep silent from good things, but only from evil ones. For when the sinner stood against him, he said: “We are cursed, and we bless; we are blasphemed, and we entreat” (1 Corinthians 4:12–13).

This man, however, brought forth neither good nor evil: “I was silent,” he says, “even from good things.” And my pain was renewed—that is, I was stirred by new [Col. 0379B] insults and new sufferings.

But because he said, “so that I would not sin with my tongue,” his heart grew hot within him, and in his meditation the genuine fire burned, the fire that inflames the movement of an innocent conscience.

At last, however, I spoke and said to the Lord: “Make known to me my end, so that I may know how long I shall be a reproach to the fool.” He also considered this: that every living man is subject to vanity. Each person, although he passes by like an image, is anxious and stores up treasures, not knowing for whom he gathers them.

But what reason was there for him, while speaking of the man who provoked him to quarrel by his dispute, suddenly to turn to the man who stores up treasure? Clearly, there would be no quarrel in the world if one person did not wish to become richer than another, whether in wealth or in honors.

But this man who guards his ways says: “My expectation [Col. 0379C] is none other than the Lord, and he himself is my substance. May he rescue me from all my iniquities and remove his scourges from me.”

“For because of the strength of the Lord’s hand I failed under rebukes,” he says, considering the strength of God’s patience, who stretched out his hands even to the cross. While I desire to imitate him, I failed under rebukes.

“Because of transgression you corrected the first man.” He had been made so that, through obedience, he might become immortal; through disobedience he became mortal. When he became mortal, his soul wasted away like a spider’s web.

He did not say, “You caused him to die,” but “You caused him to waste away,” and he gives the comparison with a spider so that, just as its web is torn apart by a sudden breath, so, when his body is torn apart by death, his soul may waste away, possessing no bodily bloom. Yet he is troubled in vain, although he knows that he [Col. 0379D] will die not long afterward.

While rebuking another in this way, he corrects himself. With tears he prays that the Lord will not be silent, but will speak in his heart and in his counsel, so that he may understand that he is a resident alien and a stranger in this world and may say: “Forgive me my sins here, so that I may recover my breath there.”

“Here,” he says, “forgive me before I depart. For if you forgive me here, I shall find refreshment there, and I will no longer be a stranger, because I will become a citizen with the saints and a member of God’s household,” through our Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns forever and ever. Amen.

# PSALM XXXIX

*For the end; a psalm of David.*

I waited patiently for the Lord, and he inclined toward me. He [Col. 0380A] heard my prayers and brought me out of the pit of misery and from the mud of filth. He set my feet upon a rock and directed my steps. He put a new song into my mouth, a hymn to our God.

Many will see, fear, and hope in the Lord. Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord and who has not turned toward vanities and false insanities.

You have done many things, O Lord my God; your wonders and your thoughts are beyond comparison with you. I proclaimed and spoke; they were multiplied beyond number.

You did not desire sacrifice or offering, but you perfected ears for me. You did not ask for a burnt offering or a sacrifice for sin. Then I said: “Behold, I come.”

In the head of the book it is written of me, that I should do your will, O my God. I desired it, and your law is in the midst of my heart.

I proclaimed your righteousness in the great assembly. Behold, [Col. 0380B] I will not restrain my lips; you know it, O Lord. I did not hide your righteousness in my heart; I spoke of your truth and your salvation. I did not conceal your mercy and your truth from the great assembly.

But you, O Lord, do not remove your mercies far from me. Your mercy and your truth have always received me.

For evils without number have surrounded me; my iniquities have seized me, and I could not see. They have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head, and my heart has abandoned me.

May it please you, O Lord, to deliver me; O Lord, look upon my help. Let those who seek my life in order to take it be put to shame and confounded together. Let those who desire evil for me turn back and be put to shame. Let those who say to me, “Well done, well done,” immediately bear their shame.

Let all [Col. 0380C] who seek you rejoice and be glad in you, and let those who love your salvation always say: “The Lord is magnified.”

But I am a beggar and poor; the Lord is concerned for me. You are my helper and my protector; my God, do not delay.

## Commentary

In the thirty-eighth psalm he said: “What is my expectation? Is it not the Lord?” Now, in the thirty-ninth, he says: “I waited patiently for the Lord, and he looked upon me.” And where he had said, “Hear my prayer,” here he says, “He heard my prayer.”

What did you pray for? “This,” he says, “is what I prayed for: that he would bring my thoughts out of the pit of misery and from the mud of lusts, which are rightly called filth, and that he would set my feet upon a rock, so that I would [Col. 0380D] no longer be shaken by the winds”—that is, by unclean spirits making suggestions.

After doing these things, may he direct my steps. Then he will give a new song to my mouth. Everyone who conquers sings a new song. But he does not sing it to himself, as though salvation answered without God, nor to Pharaoh. He sings a hymn to God, because in him we will perform valiantly, and he himself brings our enemies to nothing.

Therefore, while waiting for the Lord, I obtained this. Many will see that I have reached my desire by hoping in the Lord; they too will fear God and hope in the Lord.

Only that man is blessed who, believing that the name of the Lord is his hope, does not turn toward the vanities of the world or the false insanities of the devil. The Lord has done many wonders, and no one [Col. 0381A] is like him in his thought, either in heaven or on earth.

But I proclaimed that I had waited for the Lord, and I spoke because he had looked upon me. Those who would wait for the Lord were multiplied. For they learned from me that you did not desire sacrifice or offering, but perfected ears for me.

For you said: “Obedience of the ears is greater than the sacrifice of the hands.” You did not at all ask that a sacrifice be offered to you for sin. Then I said: “Behold, I will come.”

“In the head of the book it is written of me”—that is, at the beginning of the Psalter it is written of me that I should become a blessed man, that I should do your will, and that my will should be in your law. This I desired, and your law is in the midst of my heart.

I proclaimed your righteousness in the great assembly—that is, I spoke righteously in the assembly of the great; I judged righteously, showing partiality to no one.

I restrained my lips so that I would not hide what is [Col. 0381B] just in my heart, but spoke your truth in judgment and your salvation in the person of the humble. I said: “I have not concealed your mercy, but have said that mercy should be shown to the poor.” Nor did I remain silent about your truth in the great synagogue—that is, in the assembly of many.

Therefore, O Lord, do not remove your mercies far from me, because your mercy and your truth have always received me. Equity receives me as its own when I judge; mercy comes to my aid.

Because adversities and evils have seized me as I flee, and I cannot be present to myself, and they multiply beyond the hairs of my head, so that my own heart abandons me, I beseech you: May it please you, O Lord, to rescue me. O Lord, look upon my help.

For unclean spirits seek my soul in order to take it, and they [Col. 0381C] desire evil for me, so that, when they have satisfied themselves, they say to me: “Well done, well done.”

Grant that whenever they wish to seize me, they may immediately bear their own shame. But let those who love your salvation in me rejoice. And because I am needy in strength and poor in virtue, and cannot fight without your help, you, O Lord, help me.

They hasten to kill me; O Lord my God, do not delay in resisting them, you who reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit throughout all ages. Amen.

# PSALM XL

*For the end; a psalm of David.*

Blessed is the one who understands concerning the needy and the poor; on the evil day the Lord will deliver him. The Lord will preserve him and give him life; he will make him blessed upon the earth [Col. 0381D] and will not hand him over to the desire of his enemies.

The Lord will bring him help upon his bed of pain; you have turned his whole bed in his sickness.

I said: “O Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, because I have sinned against you.” My enemies spoke evil against me: “When will he die, and his name perish?”

And if he entered to see me, his heart spoke vainly; he gathered iniquity for himself. He went outside and spoke the same things. All my enemies whispered against me; they thought evil against me. They established an evil word against me: “Will one who sleeps not rise again?”

Indeed, the man of my peace, in whom I hoped, who ate my bread, magnified his deception against me.

But you, O Lord, have mercy on me, and I [Col. 0382A] will repay them. By this I know that you have desired me: that my enemy will not rejoice over me. But you have received me because of my innocence and established me in your presence forever.

Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from age to age. Let it be; let it be.

## Commentary

Everyone knows that there are five senses in a human being: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. But set over all these is understanding, which grows strong through the nourishment of wisdom and is made rich by the food of memory.

Accordingly, at the beginning of this psalm the person is urged to understand concerning the needy and the poor. Everyone can see him, but unless he understands concerning the needy and the poor, he will not be blessed, and on the evil day [Col. 0382B] the Lord will not deliver him.

For this needy and poor man says here as well: “I was hungry, and you did not give me food; I was thirsty, and you did not give me drink; I was a stranger, and you did not welcome me; I was sick, and you did not visit me” (Matthew 25:35–36).

Blessed, therefore, is the one who understands that the needy and poor man is Christ. If he understands that it is Christ himself, he will not hesitate but will be ready to come to his aid.

On the evil day, therefore, when it must be said to the goats, “Go into the eternal fire” (Matthew 25:41), the Lord delivers him. He preserves him, gives him life, makes him blessed, cleanses his soul on the earth, and does not hand him over into the hands of his enemy.

“And you have turned his whole bed in his sickness.” We consider the enemy’s every temptation to be meant here. We assert that his bed is prayer, upon which he cries out to the Lord: “Have mercy on [Col. 0382C] me; heal my soul, because I have sinned against you.”

When the soul has been healed, therefore, his bed—that is, his prostration—is turned in his sickness, that is, it is turned toward the one who made the soul weak before its enemies.

Thus it follows: “My enemies spoke evil against me: when will he die?” Through sin, the thing called “Christian” has perished from him. This is the name that the demons strive to make perish from us.

They enter our heart to see whether we consent. If we consent, they whisper together and think evil against us. They think an evil word against us so that, if we sin, we may not repent, but, despairing of recovery, may give ourselves as prey to our enemies, saying to them: “Will one who sleeps not rise again?”

Indeed, “the man of my peace, in whom I hoped”—that is, my outer man—has increased [Col. 0382D] his deception against me by consenting to their subjection. He who ate the bread of life with me himself consented to them. Like Judas, he accepted silver from them and betrayed the Lord.

So this man accepted lust from them and betrayed me. But you, O Lord, just as you raised your Son from the dead, so raise me from the sinner. Raise me, and I will repay them.

By this I know that you suffered for me, so that my enemy would not rejoice over me. You desired to be with me; you did not even refuse to die for me. While you lay in the tomb, I was afraid; but when you rise, my enemy will not rejoice over me. For because of my innocence you received me.

Here he speaks of the Church in the apostles and prophets. For it was not philosophers [Col. 0383A] and rhetoricians, but country people and fishermen, who were received by God and prepared the Church, which he established in his presence forever.

To her we say: “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from age to age; let it be, let it be.”

Let it not offend you, diligent reader, that we have drawn a mystical matter toward a moral interpretation. Just as the Pharisees surrounded Judas in order to make him betray the Lord and, by offering him gifts, made him surrender his salvation, so unclean spirits surround my outer man, who eats my bread, and offer him now money through greed, now luxury through lust.

If he accepts from them, he betrays. After he has betrayed, they deal with him so that he may hang himself by a noose—that is, so that he may despair of being freed through repentance. But to the righteous he says: “Will [Col. 0383B] one who sleeps not rise again?”

As I said, the mystical sense reveals this concerning the Lord’s resurrection. But from the mystical sense we have derived a moral point: because we ourselves have harmed ourselves and are cast down, let us cease harming ourselves and become innocent, so that each person may rightly say to God:

“Because of my innocence you received me. You who had cast me away from your presence because of sin now, through repentance, establish me in your presence forever,” you who reign forever and ever. Amen.

# PSALM XLI

*For the end; an understanding of the sons of Korah; a psalm of David.*

As the deer longs for springs of water, so my soul longs for you, O God. My soul thirsted for God, the living fountain. When shall I come and appear [Col. 0383C] before the face of God?

My tears have been my bread day and night, while it is said to me every day: “Where is your God?” I have remembered these things and poured out my soul within me, because I shall pass into the place of the wondrous tabernacle, even to the house of God, amid the voice of exultation and confession, the sound of one feasting.

Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, because I will yet confess to him, the salvation of my face and my God.

My soul is troubled within me; therefore I will remember you from the land of the Jordan and from Hermoniim, from the little mountain. Deep calls to deep at the sound of your cataracts. All your heights and your waves have passed over me.

By day the Lord commanded his mercy, and by night his song. With me is prayer to the God of my life; I will say to God: “You are my defender.”

Why have you [Col. 0383D] forgotten me, and why do I walk sorrowfully while the enemy afflicts me? While my bones are being crushed, those who trouble me, my enemies, reproach me. Every day they say to me: “Where is your God?”

Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, because I will yet confess to him, the salvation of my face and my God.

## Commentary
As a stag, having fed on the flesh of serpents and boiling with poison, hastens to the springs, so my soul, having been fed on the counsel of the ancient serpent, hastens to you, O God. And because through my transgression you cast me away from your presence, now through my repentance my tears are bread by day and night, as I say, “When shall I come and appear before the face of God?” For I suffer the insults of demons saying to me, “Where is the one in whose likeness you were made? He cast you out of his paradise.” But I believe that I shall enter there, into the place of the wondrous tabernacle, where the human being was made; and I shall not merely return there through Christ, but shall also arrive at the house of that very God. And I, who was cast out from there in the voice of tribulation, shall return in the voice of exultation and confession, the sound of one feasting.

Therefore, do not now be sad, O soul, but hope in God, because I shall confess him. God my Savior, the restorer of my face—that is, of his own image—will be my God. He did not cast me away from his presence as he himself desired, but I myself troubled my soul; I myself injured it. My soul was troubled, and for this reason I shall remember your name at the land of the Jordan; there I shall receive remission of sins.

Where the abyss calls to abyss: the Son calls upon the Father from the depth of the earth and of the river, while the cataracts of heaven are opened and the Holy Spirit descends; the Father calls upon the Son from the height of the heavens. Therefore, when height cries out to height, the exalted things of God have entered into me. For it was the human being who was restored, not an angel nor any other creature, when the Lord commanded his mercy by day, freely remitting sins in baptism; and he revealed that same mercy to me, who was placed in the darkness of sins as though in the obscurity of night.

For he is more merciful toward the penitent than toward the believer: there, through the grace of baptism, forgiveness is simple; here it is doubled and, as though by a twofold light, it is revealed, when a person says to God with tears, “You are my protector. Why have you forgotten me, when you are able to come to my aid by forgiving me? Why have you rejected me, when you are able to recall the expelled exile to his homeland? And why do I go about sorrowful, when you are able to restore joy?”

“I go about sorrowful,” he says, “while the enemy afflicts me, while he crushes all my bones.” For, as Solomon says, “Sorrow of heart dries up the bones” (Prov. XVII, 25). Therefore, let sorrow cease, and stop troubling me; for through hope I am made safe, and my God will be the salvation of my face, restoring freedom to my countenance. He reigns for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XLII

**For the end; a psalm of David.**

Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from an unholy nation; deliver me from an unjust and deceitful man. For you are God, my strength. Why have you rejected me, and why do I go about sorrowful while the enemy afflicts me? Send forth your light and your truth; they themselves have led me to your holy mountain and to your tabernacles. And I shall go in to the altar of God, to God who gives joy to my youth. I shall confess to you on the harp, O God, my God. Why are you sad, O my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I shall yet confess him, the salvation of my face and my God.

## COMMENTARY

The unholy nation consists of the seeds of the worst thoughts, which become the weeds sown by the evil man over the good seed in the Gospel. Deliver me from this unjust man—that is, the devil—because you are God, my strength. Do not reject me from yourself, so that I may not go about sorrowful when the enemy afflicts me. Instead, send your light and conquer my darkness; send your truth and conquer my lies.

For your light and your truth themselves lead me to your holy mountain and to your tabernacles, when you make me enter the altar of God. There, although I may have come exhausted by old age, I shall become young, so that, like an infant, I may confess to the Lord my God on the harp.

Do not now be sad, O my soul; stop troubling me; remove despair from yourself and hope in God, for I shall confess him. My God will be the salvation of my face, he who reigns for ever and ever. Amen.

[Col. 0385B]

## PSALM XLIII

**For the end; for the sons of Korah; a psalm of David for understanding.**

O God, we have heard with our ears; our fathers have declared to us the work that you performed in their days and in ancient times. Your hand destroyed nations, and you planted them; you afflicted peoples and expelled them. For they did not possess the land by their own sword, nor did their own arm save them, but your right hand and your arm, and the illumination of your face, because you were pleased with them.

You are yourself my King and my God, who commands salvation for Jacob. In you we shall scatter our enemies with the horn; in your name we shall despise those who rise up against us. For I shall not hope in my bow, and my sword will not save me. For you saved us from those who afflicted us, and you put to shame those who hated us.

In God we shall praise him all day long, and in your name we shall confess for ever. But now you have rejected us and put us to shame, and you do not go out with our powers. You have turned us back before our enemies, and those who hate us plundered us for themselves. You gave us like sheep for food, and you scattered us among the nations. You sold your people for no price, and there was no multitude in their exchanges.

You made us a reproach to our neighbors, mockery and derision to those around us. You made us a likeness to the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples. All day long my shame is before me, and confusion of face has covered me, at the voice of one reproaching and reviling, at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten you, nor have we acted wickedly against your covenant. Our heart did not turn back, and you turned our paths away from your way. For you humbled us in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death covered us.

If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have stretched out our hands to a foreign god, will not God investigate this? For he himself knows the secrets of the heart. For on your account we are put to death all day long; we are regarded as sheep for slaughter.

Rise up. Why do you sleep, O Lord? Rise up, and do not reject us forever. Why do you turn your face away and forget our poverty and our affliction? For our soul has been humbled in the dust; our belly has clung to the earth. Rise up, O Lord; help us and redeem us for the sake of your name.

[Col. 0386A]

## COMMENTARY

Three kinds of enemies rise up against the Christian: one kind is the devil and his demons; another is persecutors; the third is common to all, the savagery of barbarians. But all three kinds are conquered neither by our bow nor by our arm, but by the right hand of God and by the illumination of his face, of whom our fathers told us how his hand expelled the nations and planted them.

Therefore, just as they did not possess the land by their own sword, so we, not trusting in our own strength, possess the land of our body. Rather, you save us from those who afflict us, whether perfidious kings, demons, or—as I have said—our customary enemies, because we are handed over to them for our sins, like sheep for slaughter.

But if we cry out, saying, “All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten you, O Lord”; or if we have forgotten the name of our God, or if we have stretched out our hands to foreign gods, you, the true God, investigate these things, for you know best the hidden things of the heart.

Whatever adversity every holy person endures, he suffers for God. For just as one who possesses much money, if he suffers the sword, suffers for the sake of his money, so one who possesses holiness in his conduct suffers for God whatever adversity he may endure. This is the highest integrity of holiness. He suffers the enemy, whether a persecutor of the faith, a bodily persecutor of the world, or the ruler of this world himself and his ministers.

Therefore, holding fast to holiness, let us cry out to the Lord: “For on your account we are afflicted with death all day long.” We ask you to rise up and not reject us forever, lest you forget our poverty and our affliction, for our soul has been humbled in the dust, and our belly has clung to the earth.

For when we are weighed down by bodily needs, our soul is tormented in the dust. But when our belly clings to earthly foods, it threatens us with eternal destruction. We show you our wounds; you who are the Savior, provide medicines for our wounds.

No one will have a soul freed from the humility of dust unless you grant the soul, through an invisible gift, contempt for bodily dust. Nor will anyone have love of fasting and prayer for the purpose of despising the belly that clings to the earth, unless you grant it.

Rise up, O Lord; help us and free us, for this very reason: because we are reckoned by the splendor of your name. Free us from the occupations of dust in which our soul is humbled, and from the burden of the belly. For if you grant us the gifts of these two forms—contempt for the body and for the belly—we shall be free in Christ Jesus our Lord, through whom and with whom honor and glory belong to you, O God the Father, and to the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XLIV

**For the end; for those who will be changed; for the sons of Korah; for understanding; a song for the Beloved.**

My heart has poured forth a good word; I speak my works to the king. My tongue is the pen of a swiftly writing scribe. You are beautiful in form beyond the sons of men; grace has been poured forth upon your lips. Therefore God has blessed you for ever.

Gird your sword upon your thigh, O most powerful one. In your appearance and your beauty, set your mind; go forth prosperously and reign. Because of truth and gentleness and righteousness, your right hand will lead you wondrously.

Your arrows are sharp; peoples shall fall beneath you, in the hearts of the enemies of the king. Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; the rod of uprightness is the rod of your kingdom. You have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions.

Myrrh, liquid perfume, and cassia are from your garments, from ivory houses, by which the daughters of kings delighted you in your honor. The queen stood at your right hand, clothed in gold, surrounded with variety.

Hear, O daughter, and see; incline your ear, and forget your people and your father’s house. And the king shall desire your beauty, for he himself is the Lord your God, and they shall adore him. And the daughters of Tyre shall entreat your face with gifts, all the rich among the people.

All the glory of the king’s daughter is within; she is clothed with varieties, surrounded by golden borders. Virgins shall be brought to the king after her; her companions shall be brought to you. They shall be brought with joy and exultation; they shall be led into the temple of the king.

In place of your fathers, sons have been born to you; you shall appoint them princes over all the earth. They shall remember your name, O Lord, throughout every generation and generation. Therefore peoples shall confess you for ever and ever.

## COMMENTARY

The heart of the Father poured forth the good Word; “all things were made through him” (John I), because all things acknowledge him as their Creator. His works speak to their king—that is, all that we are, in which we subsist and move and exist, are your works.

“My tongue is a pen.” Whose pen? “Of a scribe,” he says, “writing swiftly.” Let us hear what the prophet’s tongue wishes to utter in agitation and haste. “This Word,” he says, “which the Father poured forth, whose works are all that we are, will appear beautiful in form and will rule over the sons of men. Beautiful in form—that is, he will be born in a virginal form.”

And grace will proceed from his lips, through which he will be blessed for ever. And he girds his sword upon his thigh, to cut off all lusts. Showing his appearance—that is, making the Father manifest—and his beauty—that is, the Holy Spirit. For the Father is the appearance of the Son, and the Holy Spirit is his beauty. In these he fixes his purpose, proceeds prosperously, and reigns because of truth.

Because of this truth he descended from heaven, for it had perished from the sons of men. For this truth proceed and reign. And not only because of truth, but also because of gentleness and righteousness, the Trinity reigns.

For these three qualities in Christ: because of truth, the Father is the Father of truth; because of gentleness, the Son, who emptied himself and, although he was equal to the Father, took the form of a servant (Phil. II), in which he appeared beautiful; and because of his righteousness, the Holy Spirit. For he says to John when he was baptized, “Thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness” (Matt. III). After these words the heavens were opened, and the Holy Spirit came upon him in the form of a dove.

After this, his right hand led him wondrously; by it he gave sight to the blind, cured the sick, and raised the dead. His arrows are sharp, as is known to all, so that the lovers of this world themselves depicted the unclean spirit in the form of Cupid, drawing a bow and shooting arrows that wound people with the love of lust.

Thus our Lord will shoot extremely powerful sharp arrows into the love of the kingdom of heaven, so that people will renounce father and mother and everything they possess; moreover, they will deny themselves and follow him.

These arrows free the friends of the king and kill the enemies of the king. For they are struck in the heart, where the arrows find their suggestions. When these arrows have won victory in our heart, then we receive Christ’s seat in our mind, and we desire his straight rod—that is, the rule of right faith—the rod of his kingdom. Under its discipline we love righteousness and hate iniquity, imitating the one whom God anointed with the oil of gladness beyond his companions.

For just as he appeared beautiful in form when he was born in the flesh beyond the sons of men, so Christ Jesus appeared anointed with chrism beyond all others. Many holy sons of men existed from Abel until Christ, but none was born from a Virgin; none was brought forth in this appearance or manifested in this form.

“Who,” he says, “will be like God among the sons of God?”—so that we may understand: those are sons by grace; this one is Son by nature. Many are christs through anointing with oil, but this one is Christ beyond all participants: with angels adoring, stars announcing, prophets proclaiming, John fearing, the heavens opened, the Father crying out from heaven, and the Holy Spirit coming from heaven and remaining in him. He is Christ beyond all those who share in the name that has been shared with them.

“Myrrh, liquid perfume, and cassia are from his garments.” Myrrh signifies the assumption of the body. Liquid perfume signifies that people were saved by touching his garments. Cassia signifies that the fragrance of life is approved by believers.

Against this comes the statement that Judas touched his garment and perished. The soldiers, moreover, possessed his garment, and for this very reason they too were brought down to destruction. How, then, was the salvation of the soul produced by the fragrance of his garments? Hear the Apostle saying: “To some, an odor of life unto life; to others, an odor of death unto death” (II Cor. II).

It should also be considered that ivory houses delight him. An ivory house is a chaste body in which the moth of any sinful lust does not work. Therefore it is said to the soul, into whose power the body has been given: “Hear, daughter, and see; incline your ear” to these words, so that you may forget your people—that is, the examples of sinners—and the house of your father—that is, the imitation of your father Adam according to the flesh.

Why this? Because the king desired your beauty. Who is this king? “The one whom,” he says, “the daughters of Tyre adore with gifts.” If Tyre, which was always more superstitious than the other cities, gives souls adoring Christ and offering gifts, how much more will all the rich among the people adore his face?

Indeed, all the glory that queens display outwardly in jewels, for people to see, he wishes all the glory of the king’s daughter to be within, in the inner chambers of the mind; there he wishes her to be surrounded with varieties of virtues in golden borders.

Then virgins will be brought: incorrupt faith, patience, and prudence. Their companions will be brought with them in joy and exultation, so that they may enter the temple of the king.

In place of the twelve patriarchs, twelve other sons have been born to God, whom Jesus appointed princes over all the earth, remembering his name among every nation, when he said to them, “Baptize all nations” (Mark XVI). Therefore peoples confess God for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XLV

**For the end; for the sons of Korah; concerning hidden things.**

Our God is our refuge and strength, a helper in tribulations that have found us exceedingly. Therefore we shall not fear when the earth is shaken and the mountains are transferred into the heart of the sea. Its waters roared and were troubled; the mountains were shaken by his power.

The rush of the river gladdens the city of God; the Most High sanctified his tabernacle. God is in the midst of it; it shall not be moved. God will help it at the break of dawn. Nations were troubled and kingdoms were inclined; he gave his voice, and the earth was moved.

The Lord of hosts is with us; our protector is the God of Jacob. Come and see the works of the Lord, what wonders he has placed upon the earth. He will remove wars to the ends of the earth. He will break the bow and shatter the weapons, and burn the shields with fire.

Be still and see, for I am God. I shall be exalted among the nations, and I shall be exalted on the earth. The Lord of hosts is with us; our protector is the God of Jacob.

## COMMENTARY

When you have poured out a prayer to God in tears and the tribulation of your soul, be confident that God becomes for you both a refuge and a strength. You begin not to fear when the earth of your body is shaken.

For the mountains are transferred: the apostles of the Lord, proclaiming his height, are transferred into the heart of the sea, into the minds of the fluctuating world, however much its waters may roar and be troubled. Even the mountains themselves are troubled—that is, the apostles—in his power, that is, in his passion.

However great the sins that trouble souls may be, and however much those oppressed by the consciousness of sins may be afflicted when the apostles preach, a single rush of the Jordan grants remission of sins and gladdens the city of God, when the Holy Spirit sanctifies the tabernacle of your body.

God will no longer be shaken in you, when God helps your soul by his gaze. The Hebrew says, “God helped him at the break of dawn,” that is, when the darkness of sins has passed through the rush of the river, God, who is light, gives the beginning of light to his heart and helps it—that is, the soul that says, “The Lord of hosts is with us; our protector is the God of Jacob.”

However much the nations may be troubled—that is, those who worship idols against the martyrs of the Lord—and however much kingdoms may incline toward persecuting them, the Most High gives his voice in their hearts. Thus the earth of their bodies is moved that they do not fear at all those who kill the body, but fear him who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.

They so despise their own souls that by their sufferings they break their bows and shatter their weapons. Who does this? Those who are free from all the cares of the world and see that he is God who is denied by the nations and crucified by the Jews. He is our refuge, our strength, our helper, the God of hosts, and our protector. He is also the God of Jacob, reigning with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and for all ages of ages. Amen.

## PSALM XLVI

**For the end; for the sons of Korah; a psalm of David.**

All nations, clap your hands; shout joyfully to God with a voice of exultation. For the Lord is most high and terrible, a great king over all the earth. He subjected peoples to us and nations beneath our feet. He chose for us his inheritance, the beauty of Jacob whom he loved.

God ascended with a shout of joy, and the Lord with the sound of a trumpet. Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises to our king, sing praises. For God is king of all the earth; sing praises wisely.

God shall reign over the nations; God sits upon his holy throne. The princes of the peoples have gathered with the God of Abraham, for the strong gods of the earth have been greatly exalted.

## COMMENTARY

“All nations, clap your hands.” Just as, at the coming of the devil, mourning was imposed upon all nations—for we heard a voice from heaven saying, “Woe to the earth and the sea, because the devil has been cast down to you” (Rev. XII)—so, at the coming of the Lord Jesus, it is said with a voice of exultation: “All nations, clap your hands.”

For this is the Most High God, the terrible God, who is great over all the earth. He subjected peoples to us. The apostles say this: “He subjected peoples to us, and nations beneath our feet.”

When did he do this? When he chose for us his inheritance in the form of Mary, whom the Holy Spirit loved. Then he ascended amid clamor and with the sound of a trumpet. Herod is troubled, the shepherds are frightened, the magi flee, infants are killed, and the angels sing praises, saying, “Glory to God in the highest.” They say to the shepherds, “Behold, God reigns over all nations; God sits upon his holy throne.”

If his throne is wherever unviolated virginity has been preserved, how much more was it in Mary?

“The princes of the peoples gathered with the God of Abraham.” In this passage he indicates the angels, who came with the God of Abraham to Mary when they sang his glory.

But let us hear why the great king was born and why the princes gathered with the God of Abraham. “For this reason,” he says, “they gathered, because the strong gods of the earth had been greatly exalted in their superstitions and temples.” After these had been expelled and cast down, the Lord Jesus Christ would reign over all nations for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XLVII

**A song psalm for the sons of Korah, the second day of the week.**

Great is the Lord and exceedingly worthy of praise, in the city of our God, on his holy mountain. Mount Zion is founded as the exultation of the whole earth; its northern slopes are the city of the great king. God will be known in its houses when he receives it.

For behold, the kings of the earth gathered; they came together as one. When they saw, they were so astonished; they were troubled and shaken; trembling seized them. There were pains like those of a woman in labor. With a violent wind you will crush the ships of Tarshish.

As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God. God founded it for ever. We have received your mercy, O God, in the midst of your temple. According to your name, O God, so also is your praise to the ends of the earth. Your right hand is full of righteousness.

Let Mount Zion rejoice, and let the daughters of Judah exult because of your judgments, O Lord. Surround Zion and embrace it; recount it in its towers. Set your hearts upon its strength, and distribute its houses, so that you may declare it to the next generation: “For this is our God for ever and ever; he himself will rule us for all ages.”

## COMMENTARY

“Great is the Lord and exceedingly worthy of praise.” The Lord’s praise must be proclaimed according to the diversity of his gifts and works. He is praised in the saints; he is praised in the gifts of bodily and spiritual food; he is praised in the making of the world and in the various gifts of his immeasurable mercy, as we have said.

But for what reason is he praised in this psalm? “Because,” he says, “he enlarged the exultation of the whole earth from Mount Zion, from the northern side.” There is the city of the great king, the city of Bethlehem.

In the serious people of this city—that is, those who are not superfluous through any lightness—he was known when he received it. What did he receive? The exultation, certainly, which he enlarged over the whole earth. To the serious he is known even to this day. For just as, if you see someone frivolous and vain, you recognize the devil there, so if you see someone distinguished by seriousness, you recognize the Lord Jesus Christ there.

Thus he was then known among the serious: in Mary’s integrity and Joseph’s chastity. Immediately, however, when he was known in them, the kings of the earth were troubled. The chief priests and scribes of the people came to the king, and, questioned about the indication of the star, they said that Christ had been born in Bethlehem of Judah. Then, he says, “the king was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him” (Matt. II).

They too, when they saw the star, were astonished, and trembling seized them, so that, warned in a dream, they did not return to King Herod. But the king sent and killed all the infants, and there the mothers mourned their deaths, as women in labor had mourned. They mourned in a violent spirit.

The ships of Tarshish were also crushed. He made an etymology by naming the ships of Tarshish, because at the time when the Lord was not found and the infants were killed, even the royal vessels were harassed at the king’s command. The magi, who had not returned to the king, believed that they might have been able to flee in them.

But we, just as we heard from them that the King had been born, so also saw him in the city of our God, which the Lord founded for ever. There we receive your mercy, O God, in the midst of your temple, according to your name by which you are called Savior. Thus also is your praise to the ends of the earth, for your right hand is full of righteousness, by which you deem us worthy to be rescued and to subdue the devil.

When this has been done, Mount Zion rejoices, the Church rejoices, and the daughters of Judah exult: all the souls brought forth from the womb of the Church through a repeated birth. They exult because of your judgments, O Lord, by which you judged that the devil should be subdued and human souls set free.

Now you, O souls who have been freed and born again, surround your mother Zion, and drink from the breasts of the two Testaments, full of milk. Proclaim in her towers the mercy that you have received. Those who are in the towers defend the city and resist its enemies.

Set your hearts upon her strength. Consider with what strength she fights for you, and distribute her steps: let each person approach his step according to his merit, so that to one you may justly hand over the episcopal seat and to another the rank of the presbyterate. Distribute her steps without money and without partiality, so that you may declare it to the next generation.

For this is the Lord our God, the Son of God, who reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit; he himself will rule us for all ages. Amen.

## PSALM XLVIII

**For the end; for the sons of Korah; a psalm of David.**

Hear this, all nations; receive it with your ears, all who inhabit the world. You earthborn and sons of men alike, rich and poor together. My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart understanding. I shall incline my ear to a parable; I shall open my proposition on the psaltery.

Why should I fear in an evil day, when the iniquity of my heel surrounds me? Those who trust in their strength and glory in the abundance of their riches. A brother does not redeem—shall a human being redeem? He will not give God his propitiation, nor the price of the redemption of his soul.

He will labor for ever and still live to the end. He will not see destruction when he sees the wise dying; together the foolish and the senseless will perish. And they will leave their riches to others, and their graves will be their houses for ever. Their dwellings will be from generation to generation; they called their names in their lands.

And a human being, when he was in honor, did not understand; he was compared to foolish beasts and became like them. This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them, and afterward they will be pleased in their own speech. Like sheep they are placed in hell; death will feed upon them. And the just will rule over them in the morning, and their help will grow old in hell, away from their glory.

Yet God will redeem my soul from the hand of the underworld, when he receives me. Do not fear when a person becomes rich and when the glory of his house is multiplied. For when he dies, he will take nothing, nor will the glory of his house descend with him.

For his soul will be blessed during his life; he will confess to you when you do good to him. He will enter unto the generation of his fathers, and for ever he will not see light. A human being, when he was in honor, did not understand; he was compared to foolish beasts and became like them.

## COMMENTARY

The voice of Christ alone calls all people together as one, excluding every respect of persons: rich and poor, noble and ignoble. It excludes no earthly summit of dignity whatsoever; it invites everyone equally, opening its proposition on the psaltery and showing what we should fear on the evil day.

“Let not,” he says, “the iniquity of my heel surround me.” In himself he says what you should fear in yourself. The heel signifies the end of the body; the serpent watches that point and lies in wait there. This alone must be feared by all: that at their end they may be caught by their own iniquity. For whatever work a person is found doing at the end, in that he will remain for ever.

But you who trust in your strength and glory in the abundance of riches, know this: no one redeems you from destruction—not father, not mother—except the human being Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a redemption for all (I Tim. II).

None of you will give God his own portion, the price of the redemption of his soul, so as to labor for ever and live to the end and not see destruction when he sees the wise dying. For if all those great, wealthy, and exceedingly wise people have died, how will the foolish not perish, those who gather riches and, wretchedly, refuse to give to the needy while they are able?

These people will leave their riches to others. Even if they have many houses, only their graves will be their houses for ever. Wretched human being! While he is in the body, he does not understand this; when he begins to die like cattle, he will become like them.

Meanwhile, in this way of life in which they live, holy admonitions are a scandal to them; afterward they will speak blessing with their mouth. When death feeds upon them as upon sheep placed in hell, then the just will rule over them in the morning, when the light of the resurrection begins, when those glorious ones who were expelled from their glory appear.

Then God will free my soul from the hand of hell, receiving me. Therefore do not fear your poverty when you look at the riches of others, which you know well must be left behind here by the dying person. For when he dies, he does not take everything with him, nor does the glory of his house descend together with him.

In the end, his soul will be blessed by flatterers during his life. Afterward he will confess unwillingly to God that, through God’s goodness, he had possessed much and had been able to do much, repenting that, although he could have helped the poor, he had not wished to.

And because a late confession does not obtain the fruit of forgiveness, at the time when he enters the generation of his fathers, having already laid aside the body, he will not see the light for ever. Why? Because, while he was in the body, he did not understand these things; now he has been compared to foolish beasts and has become like them.

Yet if you ask in what honor he had been, he was like God; and now he is like foolish beasts. For it is not while he possesses in himself the likeness of God that he will fail to see the light, but after he has cast off the likeness of God and begun, like an animal, to serve his belly and lust. Having now become like cattle, he will be as worthless to God as cattle are worthless.

And therefore the generation of the dead enters in this way, in its sins, because those whom it imitated here in this life are its fathers there—not those from whose seed they were propagated, but those whose works they imitated.

Indeed, although the Jews were sons of Abraham, the Lord says to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.” See also what he added: “You are from your father the devil, for you wish to do the works of your father” (John VIII).

Thus he enters into the generation of his fathers; for ever he will not see the light. But those who preserve the likeness of God and do not cast it away by taking upon themselves the likeness of sinners will come from east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom (Matt. VIII) of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, who reigns for ever and ever. Amen.

## PSALM XLIX

**A psalm of Asaph.**
God of gods, the Lord has spoken and summoned the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting. Out of Zion, the perfection of his beauty. Our God will come openly; our God, and he will not be silent. Fire will go before him, and a mighty tempest will rage around him. He summoned heaven above and the earth, to distinguish his people. [Col. 0394B] “Gather his holy ones to him, those who establish his covenant over sacrifices.” And the heavens will proclaim his righteousness, for God is judge.

“Hear, my people, and I will speak; Israel, and I will testify against you. I am God, your God. I will not rebuke you because of your sacrifices; your burnt offerings, however, are always before me. I will not accept calves from your house, nor goats from your flocks. For all the wild beasts of the forests are mine, as are the animals on the mountains and the cattle. I know all the birds of the heavens, and the beauty of the field is with me. If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are mine. Shall I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats? Offer to God a sacrifice of praise, and fulfill your vows to the Most High. And call upon me in the day of tribulation; I will deliver you, and you will honor me.

“But to the sinner [Col. 0394C] God said: Why do you recount my righteous acts and take my covenant upon your lips? You truly hate discipline and cast my words behind you. If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you made common cause with adulterers. Your mouth overflowed with wickedness, and your tongue wove deceit. Sitting, you spoke against your brother and laid a stumbling-block against your mother’s son. You did these things, and I was silent. You wickedly supposed that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set these things before your face. Understand this, you who forget God, lest he suddenly seize you and there be no one to deliver you. A sacrifice of praise will honor me, and there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God.”

## Commentary

“God” is not the name of God, but an indication by which [Col. 0394D] something higher cannot be indicated in human language. Wishing his worshipers to share in this name, he caused them to be called by that name—while he himself is God of gods, and those who have merited through serving him to be called by this name are so called.

When, then, did the Father speak? Or when did he summon the earth? Surely, then, when the perfection of beauty appeared from Zion. At that time he will come openly to judge the world by fire. Fire, moreover, will burn in his presence, and a mighty tempest will surround him.

Then the apostles and martyrs, the orthodox, and all the teachers who establish his covenant over sacrifices will be gathered. In the present age the apostles are admonishers and teachers. They are the heavens that proclaim the glory of God. Then, when God begins [Col. 0395A] to be judge, all those who now preach his mercy will proclaim his righteousness.

“Hear this, then, my people; hear, and I will speak. Then I testify to you that I will come to judge—the one who now came to redeem. I am indeed your God. Do not suppose that I will rebuke you because of sacrifices; I desire obedience more than sacrifice. I have decreed that my commandments be kept above sacrifices.

“For I will not eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats; whatever walks and flies is mine. Why will you offer me what is mine in place of what is yours? This is yours: if with a pure heart you pour out praises to me and fulfill the vow that you made when you entered baptism, when you promised that you would renounce the devil and vowed that you would keep my commandments.

“When you have done this, call upon me in the day of tribulation, [Col. 0395B] at the time when you depart from this body. I will deliver you from the hands of demons, and you will magnify me for my gifts.

“But you who pursue profits in order to obtain the priesthood, or you who desire human glory, or you who share in theft—even if you yourself are not an adulterer, you nevertheless live with adulterers—why do you recount my righteousness, says the Lord, while you slander your brother and lay a stumbling-block? Do you despise my silence and hope that I am like you? I will rebuke you and set these things before your face. Do not forget; repay the Lord what you promised, lest he seize you like a lion and there be no one to deliver you.

“Therefore the end must always be kept before one’s eyes, and one must remain in the praises of God. For there is the way in which the salvation of God is revealed—the God who reigns for ages of ages.” [Col. 0395C] Amen.

# PSALM L

*A psalm of David, for the end, when the prophet Nathan came to him, when he went in to Bathsheba.*

Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy. And according to the multitude of your mercies, blot out my iniquity. Wash me yet more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I know my iniquity, and my sin is always before me. Against you alone have I sinned, and I have done evil before you, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.

For behold, I was conceived in iniquities, and my mother conceived me in sins. For behold, you have loved truth; you have revealed to me the uncertain and hidden things of your wisdom. You will sprinkle me with hyssop, Lord, and I shall be cleansed; [Col. 0395D] you will wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow. You will give joy and gladness to my hearing, and the humbled bones will rejoice.

Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. Create a clean heart in me, O God, and renew a right spirit within my innermost being. Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me. Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit.

I will teach the wicked your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to you. Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will exult in your righteousness. Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise. For if you had desired sacrifice, I would surely have offered it; you will not delight in burnt offerings. A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit; a contrite and humbled heart [Col. 0396A] God will not despise.

Deal kindly, Lord, in your good pleasure with Zion, so that the walls of Jerusalem may be built. Then you will accept the sacrifice of righteousness, offering and burnt offerings; then they will place calves upon your altar.

## Commentary

When the prophet Nathan came to King David, he did not begin by accusing him of the sin, but began by demanding a judgment. He said: “I heard that you had flocks of sheep and many herds, while a poor man who possessed only one little ewe-lamb had it taken away.” Having brought the matter before the king as judge, he received the king’s sentence that the one who had done this deserved death.

Then Nathan said: “You are the man who did this. You killed Uriah the Hittite and took his wife. Thus says the Lord: The sword will not depart from [Col. 0396B] your house forever.” The sentence found the guilty man, and the king, placed beneath the accuser, laid aside his authority and was condemned by his own judgment.

For God came to him hidden in Nathan, concealed in the prophet, and through the prophet himself demanded judgment from the man. God prevailed. God was justified in his words, by which he demanded a sentence from the man; the sentence judged between the angry God and the offending man, and God prevailed when judged by the man. For the man said: “The man who did this deserves death.”

God, therefore, who wished to pronounce this sentence against the guilty man, came to judgment so that, if it had been judged that the deed ought not to be punished, he would not have been justified in his words and would not have prevailed when judged. But when it was said, “The man who did this deserves death,” God, who had come to judgment to be judged, was justified in his words [Col. 0396C] and prevailed while being judged.

Let us now see what God’s victory accomplished. It held the emperor captive and handed the guilty man over to the sentence. The guilty man fled to mercy, removed his purple robe, and put on sackcloth. He ate ashes as though they were bread and mixed tears with his drink.

“Show me, Lord,” he said, “by what deeds the sentence may be changed. For if you deign to forgive me, placed as I am in this humility, even the ungodly will turn back to you. Have mercy, I beg you, according to your great mercy, for I acknowledge my iniquity. I acknowledge that you are justly angry and that I have acted unjustly.

“Against you alone have I sinned. Everyone who lives under judgment, when he transgresses, sins against God and sins against the laws of the world. But this king, acting under no one other than God [Col. 0396D] alone and fearing God alone above his authority, sinned against God alone.

“I have done evil before you,” he says; “I did not flee from your presence. For I wanted you to judge me as an offender rather than bind me as one who was fleeing.

“I was conceived in iniquities.” In his confession he preserved the goodness of the Creator. He did not say, “My mother begot me with iniquities,” or “with sins,” but, “I was conceived in iniquities, and my mother begot me in sins.” By saying that his mother conceived him in her own iniquities and gave birth to him in the sins of the world, he marked this distinction: every sin is conceived in the heart and brought to completion by the mouth. But the one who is born bears Adam’s sentence; he does not yet possess his own sin.

“You, Lord, have loved truth,” [Col. 0397A] at the time when I fashioned falsehood so that it might be placed in a more serious conflict. You revealed to me the uncertain and hidden thing in my sins, which was in my heart—Uriah—and you revealed it to me in such a way that I pronounced the sentence against myself.

But because you commanded purification from defilement to be made by the sprinkling of hyssop, I say: “You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed; you will wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.” This will happen if you give joy to my hearing, when it is said to me: “Shepherd of sheep, I announce to you great joy, because today the Lord has been born from the seed of David according to the flesh” (Luke II; Romans I).

Behold the joy through which the humbled bones rejoice; through which, O God, you turn your face away from my sins; through which you blot out all my iniquities; through which you create a clean heart in [Col. 0397B] me, O God; through which you renew a right spirit within my innermost being, so that by spiritual desire I may exclude carnal desire, and may detest whatever is perverse as earnestly as I embrace whatever is approved as right before you.

As I make these petitions, do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me. Rather, restore to me the joy that I lost, and with the spirit that you grant to confirm forgiveness, strengthen me through that same spirit. By naming the spirit a third time, he taught that the Trinity exists in unity.

“When, then,” he says, “you have strengthened me, I too will teach the wicked your forgiveness, because you have mercy and forgive repentant sinners. And when the ungodly hear these things, they will turn back to you through repentance.

“Deliver me from bloodshed”—from that sentence in which you said: “The sword will not depart from your house” (2 Samuel XII). Deliver me from this sentence, so that my tongue may exult in your righteousness.

“As for my lips, which are closed because of my guilt, you will open them by your forgiveness. Once opened, my mouth will proclaim your praise.

“But because it is written in your law that a sacrifice should be offered for each sin, while now you do not wish to be appeased by sacrifices—which, if you desired them, I would certainly offer—because you do not delight in these, I offer you as a sacrifice a troubled spirit, a contrite and humbled heart.

“Thus may you deal kindly, in your good pleasure, with Zion; may you remove from it the sword that you established because of my sin; may its walls not be destroyed, but rather be built up.

“Then the sacrifices of righteousness will be accepted there: offerings of a troubled spirit and [Col. 0397D] burnt offerings of a humbled heart. And calves will be placed upon your altar—that is, young men who understand that you are so displeased by lust that you punish it, yet forgive the offense through the tears of a troubled spirit.

“These calves, who were beneath the vices of lust, will by their own will be placed upon your altar—that is, in the height of a chaste purpose.”
