Although we have treated only the historical meaning of the verse in which God is justified in his words and prevails when judged, this matter was fulfilled in the judgment of the Savior. He prevailed when he was judged in his passion, and he prevailed in such a way as to obtain every principality, authority, and power. Yet he is judged daily also, and while he is judged, he prevails.

For we are accustomed to say: “Why [Col. 0398A] has God done this to me? Why this? Behold, the wicked reign, while the righteous are afflicted.” He prevails when he is judged, like a physician who orders those whose recovery he despairs of to be indulged according to their wishes and commands that nothing they desire be denied them. But those whom he knows can be saved he orders to be bound, to drink bitter medicines, to be cut with the knife, and to be cauterized.

Thus, when those who are saved have abstained, and those who have died have acquiesced in their own desires, the physician will be justified in his words. It will be said to him: “We were unjustly blaming you when you bound and cut good people, while you neither cut nor afflicted the wicked, and even allowed them to enjoy their desires.”

To this we may add what is said of God: “For the Lord disciplines the one he loves” (Proverbs III). Let us ask, however, that he discipline us in his mercy, so that his judgments may help us, [Col. 0398B] through our Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns for ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM LI

*For the end; a song of understanding by David, when Doeg the Idumean came to him and reported to Saul: “David has come to the house of Ahimelech.”*

Why do you boast in wickedness, you who are powerful in iniquity? All day long your tongue devised injustice; like a sharp razor, you practiced deceit. You loved wickedness more than goodness, iniquity more than speaking righteousness. You loved every word of destruction, a deceitful tongue.

Therefore God will destroy you forever; he will tear you away and remove you from your dwelling, and your root from the land of the living. The righteous will see and fear, and they will laugh at him and say: “Behold the man who did not make God his helper [Col. 0398C] but trusted in the abundance of his riches and prevailed in his vanity.”

But I, like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, have trusted in the mercy of God forever and ever. I will give thanks to you forever, because you have done this; and I will await your name, for it is good in the presence of your holy ones.

## Commentary

David, fleeing from Saul, came to the priest Ahimelech and, finding the holy loaves, took them for himself and for those who were with him. When the priest objected, David disclosed the reason why he should not be prevented, saying: “I and my servants are clean from women” (1 Samuel XXI).

Therefore, when you flee the sword of the ruler of the world, take refuge at the altar, and, being clean, take the holy bread, [Col. 0398D] there will be someone who, at the devil’s instigation, will afflict, pursue, and expose you. Because no one other than the devil brings this about, you will sing all the words of this psalm in prayer against the devil himself, saying:

“Why do you boast in wickedness, you who are powerful in iniquity? All day”—that is, every day—you practice injustice in your thoughts. Your tongue does not cease to provide counsels against righteousness through your thoughts. Like a sharp razor practicing deceit, you weave deceptions with such sharpness that the man himself works toward his own destruction and rejoices while bringing about his downfall.

“Therefore God will destroy you forever.” When a man has brought to an end the sins that you persuaded him to commit, God will destroy you and tear you from his heart, because this is God’s dwelling, and he will tear out your root from the land of the living [Col. 0399A]—that is, from the body of those who live for God.

The righteous will see your cunning and fear the Lord; they will laugh at your suggestions and say: “In every work we ask God for help.”

But in the work that you persuade them to carry out, God is not placed there as helper. Those who do such things are without God, placing their hope in the riches of the world: if they are rich, they presume upon the riches of the world; if they are poor, they seek help from the rich of this world and not from God.

They prevail in their vanity. But when these things fail, the one who hopes in the mercy of God will be like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, hoping in his mercy forever. He will give thanks to the Lord forever for his benefits in the presence of all the holy ones of God, who reigns for ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM LII

[Col. 0399B]

*For the end; a song of understanding by David, concerning Amalek.*

The fool said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt and have become abominable in their iniquities; there is no one who does good. God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see whether there was anyone who understood or sought God. All have turned aside; together they have become useless. There is no one who does good, not even one.

Will not all who work iniquity understand this—those who devour my people like food, like bread? They have not called upon God; there they trembled with fear where there was no fear. For God scattered the bones of those who please men; they were put to shame, because God despised them.

Who will give salvation to Israel from Zion? When God turns back the captivity of his people, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad. [Col. 0399C]

## Commentary

When the Lord looked down from heaven through Jesus upon the children of men, the foolish Jewish people, seeing him, said in their heart: “There is no God.” All became corrupt; all became abominable—not by the will of God, but in accordance with their own wills—so that there was not even one among them who did good.

By saying “not even one,” he spoke of those who say of Christ, “There is no God.” For if he had spoken generally of all human beings, he would not have said that there was a people of his own, which they devour like food, like bread. These are the people who, because they have not called upon God, tremble with fear where there is no fear: in the observance of the Sabbath and in the washings of cups and pitchers.

But God scatters [Col. 0399D] the bones of those who please men. Hence our teacher Paul says: “If I still wished to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ” (Galatians I). Thus, while he was still a Jew, he showed that he had pleased men. But those who wish to please them, he says, will be put to shame, because God has despised them.

Which God? The one who gives salvation to Israel from Zion. Jacob is interpreted as “supplanter,” and Israel as “seeing God.” Therefore let Jacob rejoice, because he supplants the enemy; and let Israel exult, because the invisible God is seen face to face in his offspring—the God who reigns for ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM LIII

*For the end, in songs of understanding by David, when the Ziphites came and reported to Saul: “Is not David hidden among us?”* [Col. 0400A]

O God, save me by your name, and deliver me by your power. O God, hear my prayer; listen with your ears to the words of my mouth. For strangers have risen against me, and the strong have sought my life; they have not set God before their eyes.

For behold, God helps me, and the Lord is the protector of my life. Turn the evils back upon my enemies, and in your truth destroy them. I will sacrifice to you willingly, and I will give thanks to your name, Lord, for it is good. For you have delivered me from every tribulation, and my eye has looked down upon my enemies.

## Commentary

“O God, save me by your name.” This prayer [Col. 0400B] sets forth its reasons: “Deliver me,” he says, “because strangers have risen against me, and the strong have sought my life—those who do not set God before their eyes.”

The title indicates both who the strangers are and who those are who seek his life. He is shown to have gone to his enemies and to have wished to escape through them.

See to it, my friend, that you do not trust your enemies entirely. See to it that, placed in necessity, you do not steal and suppose that by this you can restore yourself; that you do not call what is good evil while wishing to please men; that you do not pass from virtues to vices because of some necessity. Do not trust them.

For they receive you in order to pretend to offer you a hiding-place. In fact, they wish to hand you over joyfully to the one who persecutes you. Blessed are you if you have not trusted them. But if you have trusted them, cry out that the Lord may save you for the sake of his name, [Col. 0400C] so that he may set your will free. For as long as it lies in agreement with vices, it is not free.

But when the Lord has helped you, destroyed your enemies, and delivered you from every tribulation, then you will sacrifice to him willingly, and his eye will look down upon your enemies—the one who reigns for ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM LIV

*For the end, in songs of understanding by David.*

Hear my prayer, O God, and do not despise my supplication; attend to me and hear me. I am saddened in my struggle, and I am troubled by the voice of the enemy and by the tribulation of the sinner. For they have inclined their iniquities against me, and in anger they were troublesome to me.

My heart was troubled within me, and the fear of [Col. 0400D] death fell upon me. Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me. And I said: “Who will give me wings like a dove’s? Then I will fly away and rest.”

Behold, I have gone far away in flight, and I remained in solitude. I awaited the one who saves me from faintness of spirit and from the tempest.

Bring them down, Lord; divide their tongues, for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city. Day and night they surround it; iniquity is upon its walls, and labor and injustice are within it. Usury and deceit have not ceased from its streets.

For if my enemy had cursed me, I would surely have endured it. And if one who hated me had spoken great things against me, perhaps I would have hidden myself from him. But you are a man of one mind with me, my leader and my acquaintance, who together with [Col. 0401A] me used to take sweet food. We walked in agreement in the house of God.

Let death come upon them, and let them descend alive into the underworld. For wickedness is in their dwellings, in their midst. I cried to the Lord, and the Lord will save me. Evening, morning, and midday I will recount and proclaim, and he will hear my voice.

He will redeem my soul in peace from those who approach me, for they were with me among many. God will hear and humble them, he who is before the ages. For there is no change in them, and they did not fear God. He stretched out his hand in repayment.

They polluted his covenant; they were divided from the anger of his face, and his heart drew near. His words were softened more than oil, yet they themselves are arrows.

Cast your care upon the Lord, and he will nourish you; he will not give the righteous eternal instability [Col. 0401B]. But you, O God, will lead them down into the pit of destruction. Men of blood and deceit will not halve their days; but I will hope in you, Lord.

## Commentary

The first state of one’s manner of life is that a person should be saddened by the struggle against sins and be troubled rather than delighted by the voice of the enemy and by the tribulation of sinners. Let the fear of death come upon him, lest he die in sins, and let outer darkness cover him, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth (Luke XIII; Matthew III).

But if it can be done, let him receive the wings of the soul in the Holy Spirit, like the dove descending from heaven, and fly away, escaping the hands of his enemies. Let him go far away and flee from sin; and, as though placed in solitude, let him not be entangled in any human [Col. 0401C] concerns.

Then he awaits God, who saves him from faintness and tempest, so that the Lord may bring them down and divide their tongues. For he has seen iniquity and contradiction in the city. This iniquity surrounds it day and night upon its walls—that is, the devil surrounds the soul upon its walls wherever it sets itself to resist vices.

“And usury and deceit have not ceased from its streets”—that is, in its thoughts. For if my enemy had cursed me—that is, if the devil himself had spoken evil against me—I would have hidden myself from him, since I am certain that he hates me.

But now you, a man of one mind with me, my leader and my acquaintance—that is, my man, the outer man, plainly the bodily man—who share sweet food with me at the table of the mystery, you [Col. 0401D] act against me. You take delight with my enemies in their counsels; through you they come to me. Let death come upon them.

And because by nature they are immortal, let them descend alive into the underworld, because wickedness is in their lodgings, in their midst—that is, in their suggestions, in the midst of their suggestions.

If, therefore, you cry out to the Lord and wish the Lord Jesus to hear you, you will recount to him in the evening, morning, and midday; you will confess to him and pour out prayers to him. Without doubt he will hear your voice in such a way as to deliver your soul from their warfare, from those who approach him.

Among these many, he himself will be with you—the one who humbles them, who never change and never fear God. God stretches out his hand in repayment to them, because they are the ones who [Col. 0402A], through our consent, pollute his covenant. Although they are divided from the anger of his face, because he is impassible, nevertheless his heart draws near.

They do not escape him, for they soften the words of their suggestions more than oil, yet they themselves are arrows. But you, Christian, cast your thought upon God, and he will nourish you. Do not say: “What shall I eat? What shall I drink? With what shall I be clothed?” (Matthew V).

Through these thoughts the demons themselves are arrows. The Lord will lead them into the pit of destruction if you cast your thought upon God. To you he will remove instability; but those men of blood and deceit he will not allow even to halve their days—that is, he will not allow them to carry out against you even half of what their temptations prepare, if you say with your whole heart: “I hope in you, Lord,” who reigns for ages [Col. 0402B] of ages. Amen.

# PSALM LV

*For the end; for the people who have been put far from the holy ones; in the inscription of the title, for David himself, when the foreigners seized him in Gath.*

Have mercy on me, O God, because man has trampled me down; all day long he has fought against me and afflicted me. My enemies have trampled me down all day, for many are those who wage war against me. From the height of the day I will fear; but I will hope in you.

In God I will praise my words; in God I have hoped; I will not fear what flesh can do to me. All day long they cursed my words; all their thoughts were for evil against me. They will dwell and hide themselves; they themselves will watch my heel.

As they have waited for my soul, you will save them for nothing; in anger you will crush the peoples. [Col. 0402C] O God, I have announced my life to you; you have placed my tears in your sight. As you promised, then my enemies will turn back.

On whatever day I call upon you, behold, I know that you are my God. In God I will praise the word; in the Lord I will praise my words. In God I have hoped; I will not fear what man can do to me.

My vows to you, O God, are upon me; I will repay you with praises. For you have delivered my soul from death and my feet from falling, so that I may please God in the light of the living.

## Commentary

If the foreigners seize you and drive you far from holy thoughts, cry out to God, saying: “Have mercy on me, Lord, because man has trampled me down”—plainly, the outer man. For through you [Col. 0402D] your enemies fight against you; through him they wage war against you all day.

But those who fight against you will fear if you say to God: “I, Lord, will hope in you; I will not fear what flesh can do to me.”

My enemies curse my words, saying: “This man teaches chastity; let us sow lusts in him. He preaches contempt for the world; let us implant love of money in him.” Their counsels are therefore against you and for evil. They act with such subtlety that they are hidden from you. You think that angels of God are giving counsel, but they are your enemies, watching your heel—that is, awaiting your end.

They regard your soul as worthless, so that, while it considers itself of little value, it may perish forever for the pleasure of a brief time. But while the soul [Col. 0403A] is wounded for nothing, those who wound it seem to be saved; for the victory of the enemies is the salvation of the enemies.

Therefore, lest this happen, cry out to God; announce your life to him; place your tears before him; and, as he promised—“Because he hopes in me, I will deliver him”—so may he turn your enemies back, as he promised.

Then you will know that your God is with you, and you will begin to sing praises in God and not fear what man can do to you, whether flesh or the very man who is revealed in the Gospels of Christ as having sown weeds over the wheat.

Then you will repay to the Lord your vows, which you promised when you entered baptism: that you would renounce the devil, all his pomp, and his crimes.

Then, I say, when the Lord has delivered your soul from the death of lust, your eyes from the destruction of desire, and your feet from falling, you will please him in the light of the living. This will be accomplished by the Lord Jesus Christ, through whom and with whom you have one divinity with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, before all things, now, and throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM LVI

*For the end; “Do not destroy,” by David, in the inscription of the title, when he fled from the face of Saul, king of Israel, into the cave.*

Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, because my soul has trusted in you. And in the shadow of your wings I will hope until iniquity passes away. I will cry to God Most High, to God who has done good to me. He sent from heaven and delivered me; he gave those who trampled me down over to reproach.

God sent his mercy and his truth, and delivered my soul from the midst of lion cubs. I slept while troubled. The children of men have teeth that are weapons and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword.

Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth. They prepared a snare for my feet and bent down my soul. They dug a pit before my face and fell into it.

My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready; I will sing and utter a psalm to the Lord. Rise up, my glory; rise up, psaltery and lyre; I will rise at dawn. I will give thanks to you among the peoples, Lord, and utter a psalm to you among the nations.

For your mercy has been magnified up to the heavens, and your truth up to the clouds. Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.

[Col. 0403D]

## Commentary

When you flee from the face of the ruler of this world who persecutes you, as Saul persecuted David, seek a cave—that is, arrange yourself in such a way that your enemy cannot find you. You should have your enemy in your hands, while he himself does not even see you.

This will happen if with your whole heart you say to God: “I hope in the shadow of your wings until iniquity passes away,” and cry out to God Most High. He himself sends from heaven, delivers you, and gives those who trample you down over to reproach.

If what you say to God—“My soul trusts in you”—is not false, and if you show by your deeds that you truly trust in him, then the one who trusts in him will not trust in anyone else: not in gold, not in an estate, and not in any earthly [Col. 0404A] power. Otherwise, by trusting in others while saying, “My soul trusts in you,” he lies to God.

But if he trusts in him, he delivers his soul from the midst of lion cubs, where he had slept in trouble. Wherever there is despair of recovery, the sleep of death weighs upon one. He called them lion cubs, whose teeth he declared to be weapons and arrows, and whose tongue was a sharp sword. “And among these,” he says, “I slept in trouble.”

O sleep! I believe this is the sleep of which the same Psalmist says: “My soul slumbered from weariness” (Psalm CXVIII).

Therefore, if you have a ready heart against the preparations of demons and utter a psalm to God, the snares that they themselves prepared for your soul will bind them, and they themselves will fall into the pits that they dug for you—provided that you rise at dawn with psaltery and lyre.

That is, cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor [Col. 0404B] of light (Ephesians VI). Then you will find his abundant mercy from earth to heaven; ascending to the clouds, you will find his truth. Then you will find God exalted above the heavens, because the Son of God ascended into heaven; and his glory reigns over all the earth with the Father and the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages. Amen.

# PSALM LVII

*For the end; “Do not destroy,” by David, in the inscription of the title.*

If indeed you speak righteousness, judge rightly, children of men. For in your heart you work iniquities on earth; your hands weave injustices. Sinners have been estranged from the womb; they have gone astray from the uterus; they have spoken falsehood.

Their fury is according to the likeness of a serpent, like a deaf asp that stops up its ears. It [Col. 0404C] will not hear the voice of charmers or of the enchanter who enchants wisely. God will crush their teeth in their mouth; the Lord will break the molars of lions.

They will come to nothing like water running away; he has bent his bow until they are weakened. Like wax that melts, they will be taken away; fire has fallen upon them, and they have not seen the sun.

Before our thorns can perceive the bramble, he swallows them up alive in his anger. The righteous will rejoice when he sees vengeance; he will wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.

And a man will say: “If indeed there is fruit for the righteous, indeed there is a God judging on earth.”

## Commentary
The Jews, seeing the Lord Jesus Christ rejecting empty observances and coming to the aid of people on the Sabbaths, were filled with anger against him, like the likeness of a serpent and like a deaf asp that stops up its ears. Asps are not captured by snake-charmers for this reason: they place one ear against the ground and block the other ear with the sharp point of their tail, so that they do not hear the voice of the skillful charmer. By adding “skillfully,” he showed that our charmer was the one who did not cease to charm the Jews skillfully. But they, with their ears closed, did not heed him, like deaf asps.

To these the Holy Spirit says: “If indeed you speak righteousness”—that is, if you truly act according to the Law—“judge rightly, sons of men”; declare the guilt and thus pronounce sentence. Why do your hands fashion injustice? Have you become estranged from the womb of your mother Sarah? Do you err from the womb of your father Abraham? Abraham did not do this: “If you were Abraham’s children, you would certainly do the works of Abraham” (John 8).

But now you have become estranged from the womb; you are not his children; you have gone astray from the womb. For you are the children of the one whose works you wish to do; you are from the father, the devil, speaking falsehoods. For he was a liar from the beginning and did not stand in the truth (ibid.). Why has your wickedness blinded you? The fire of wickedness has fallen upon you, and though you see, you do not see the sun of righteousness; rather, like lions, you open your mouths in a roar for his death.

But when he rises from the dead, God will crush their teeth in their mouths; the Lord will break the molars of the lions, so that they come to nothing, like water running away, against whom the Lord bends his bow until they are weakened. “Like melted wax they will be carried away.” Melted wax returns to its own nature and is restored again to its former state. Thus the Lord wishes them to be afflicted, so that they may return to their former condition.

“Before your thorns produce the rhamnus.” Thorns have this nature: they spring up more readily in a shrub than among trees. The rhamnus, however, is a thorny tree that bears no fruit at all. Therefore, before your thorns, changed into the hardness of trees and firmly rooted, remain fixed, and the barren rhamnus, as though alive, devours you, may your thorny and hardened iniquity consume you.

But because you cried out, “His blood be upon us and upon our children” (Matthew 27), he will rejoice when he sees the vengeance upon the impious, when he binds him to the gallows of the cross, so that he may take up the robber and lead him with himself into paradise. Then he will rejoice in this vengeance upon the impious. The Lord vindicates this righteous man as he prays and says, “Father, forgive them.”

But you, impious demons, will then see that there is fruit for the righteous, when you see the Son of God washing his hands in the blood of sinners. For when they, stirred up by unclean spirits, said, “He is guilty of death,” Christ stretched out his hands upon the cross and began to wash them in the blood of sinners, pouring blood from them and washing away their sins. Then every person said that there is indeed fruit for the righteous, for the Lord Jesus Christ, and that God, caring for the world, judges them on earth, aiding them by his judgment. Blessed is he throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM 58

For the end; “Do not destroy”; of David, in the inscription of the title, when Saul sent and guarded his house in order to kill him.

Deliver me from my enemies, my God, and free me from those rising up against me. Deliver me from those who work iniquity, and save me from men of blood. For behold, they have seized my soul; the mighty have rushed upon me. Neither is there iniquity of mine, nor sin, Lord; without iniquity I have run and directed my way. Rise up to meet me and see; and you, Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, attend to visiting all the nations; do not show mercy to all who work iniquity. They will return toward evening and suffer hunger like dogs, and they will go around the city. Behold, they will speak with their mouths, and a sword is on their lips, for who has heard? But you, Lord, will laugh at them and bring all the nations to nothing.

I will keep my strength for you, because you are my protector, God; my God, his mercy will come before me. God has shown me concerning my enemies: do not kill them, lest my people at some time forget. Scatter them by your strength and bring them down, my protector and Lord. The sin of their mouth, the word of their lips—let them be caught in their pride. And from the curse and from the lie they will be announced; in the completion, in the anger of completion, they will not exist. And they will know that God will rule Jacob and the ends of the earth.

They will return toward evening and suffer hunger like dogs, and they will go around the city. They themselves will be scattered to eat; if indeed they are not satisfied, they will murmur. But I will sing of your strength and exalt your mercy in the morning. For you have become my protector and my refuge on the day of my tribulation. My helper, to you I will sing psalms, because you are my protector, my God, my mercy.

## COMMENTARY

When the house of your body is commanded to be guarded by the prince of this world, so that you may be seized and killed by the sword of any sin, cry out from your inmost being: “Deliver me from my enemies, my God, for they have occupied my soul; the mighty have rushed upon me.” For I am flesh, whereas they are spirits. Why does a Christian suffer the persecutions of demons, except because he wishes to run his course without iniquity and direct his path? Therefore, “Rise up, Lord, to meet me and see,” because I desire to run without iniquity.

Those who persecute me are the ones who work iniquity, who return toward evening, suffer hunger like dogs, and go around the city. Behold, they speak with their mouths as though they were peaceful, but swords are on their lips. Yet however wise these unclean spirits consider themselves, you, Lord, will mock them. For all nations are nothing before you, whether they presume upon strength or trust in cleverness.

“My strength, I will be guarded by you,” because you are my protector, so that a human being might receive you. You received the human being so that your mercy might come before me and you might show me victory over my enemies. For this reason you do not take immortality away from them: so that, subjected to the human race, they may suffer eternal punishments, seeing all the angels worshiping the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Majesty. And he himself will destroy them, he who is my protector.

“The sin of their mouth is the word of their lips”—whether at the time when Adam was deceived, or now, when through suggestions they supply foul counsels to beautiful minds, so that human beings may be caught in pride, despising the commands of their Lord and, through the curse and lie of demons, being driven toward evil. Let the anger of your indignation come upon them, and they will not exist.

And they will know that you, God, rule over Jacob and over the ends of the earth. For the Lord rules there where earthly pleasures make an end. Then the unclean spirits will return toward evening, when they see that light is failing from our minds and darkness is increasing. Then they hunger for us like dogs and go around the city—namely, our mind.

They themselves will be scattered, hastening to devour, even to the destruction of the soul. For this is their satiety: to see the one who is fighting perish. But whoever is Christ’s servant says to the Lord: “I will sing of your powers.” I will say to my adversaries: “I do not take up weapons against you from my own strength, but I trust in the powers of my God, rejoicing in his mercy in the morning.”

We rejoice in his mercy in the morning when he has removed the darkness of sins from us and given his light in our hearts. We rejoice in his mercy because he has become our protector and our refuge on the day of tribulation. “My helper, to you I will sing psalms.” He sings psalms to God who sings with spirit and mouth. He sings psalms to God who puts into practice the things he sings and whose mind says to God without ceasing: “You are my mercy,” through which one reaches life, having escaped all the enemies who strive to kill us by the sword of our consent. From their counsels and violence the Lord Jesus Christ delivers us, he who reigns with God the Father and the Holy Spirit throughout all ages. Amen.

# PSALM 59

For the end; for those who will be changed; in the inscription of the title; to David, for instruction. When he set fire to Mesopotamia of Syria and Zobah, and Joab turned back and struck Edom in the Valley of Salt, twelve thousand.

God, you have rejected us and destroyed us; you were angry, yet you had mercy on us. You shook the earth and troubled it; heal its fractures, for it has been shaken. You have shown your people hard things; you have given us wine of compunction. You have given a sign to those who fear you, so that they may flee from the face of the bow. And that your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand and hear me.

God has spoken in his holy place: “I will rejoice and divide Shechem, and I will measure out the Valley of Booths. Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine, and Ephraim is the strength of my head. Judah is my king; Moab is the pot of my hope. Into Idumea I will extend my sandal; foreigners have been subjected to me.”

Who will lead me as far as the fortified city? Who will lead me as far as Idumea? Is it not you, God, who have rejected us and will not go forth, God, in our forces? Give us help in tribulation, for human salvation is vain. In God we will act valiantly, and he himself will bring to nothing those who trouble us.

## COMMENTARY

With the enemies struck down, he taught us to ascribe victory to the Lord: when he is angry, we are conquered; when he has mercy, we conquer. He himself moves the earth of our body and troubles it, whether by the threat of future judgment or by some blow of present destruction, for which we ask him to heal its fractures.

“For you have shown your people hard things”—the hard heart of Pharaoh in a hard work. “You have given us wine of compunction.” Wherever there is the Lord’s anger and the suffering of some affliction, either a cup of anger or wine of drunkenness is mentioned, as Jeremiah says to Jerusalem: “You have been drunk with the cup of the anger and fury of the Lord.”

At the time, therefore, when you gave us wine of compunction in Egypt, you gave a sign to those who fear you, so that they might flee from the face of the bow: when the destroyer of the firstborn saw the sign of the lamb’s blood, he would not touch them.

Now, therefore, because you are the same God who were then, save me—not by my strength, but by your right hand—and hear me. For God spoke in his holy servant Moses.

“I will rejoice and divide Shechem, and I will measure out the Valley of Booths.” He himself said: “Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine, and Ephraim is the strength of my head.” He himself said: “Judah is my king.” God spoke all these things in his holy one so that they might be fulfilled, that is, in our Lord Jesus Christ.

He spoke in his holy one in three ways. He spoke in his holy one—that is, in Jacob he spoke concerning Ephraim and Manasseh and concerning Judah. He spoke these same things in his holy one, as we said, in Moses; but in them he spoke improperly, so that in Jesus Christ they might be fulfilled not improperly but properly.

In him Judah obtained the kingdom, and there will be no end to his kingdom. “Judah, therefore, is my king; Moab is the cauldron of my hope.” A *lebes*—that is, a pot. Because Moab is the son of fornication, his lust is in the pot of burning; and because the Moabites occupied Idumea, he says: “I will cast Moab out from there, and there I will extend my sandal.”

Therefore you also, Christian, if you have driven Moab from the land he had invaded, and, having taken captive or burned the king of lust like a pot, have begun to hold the Philistines subject, the Lord will lead you into the city of those surrounding you, onto the rock of refuge in his help, where angels surround and govern you, until you reach the fortified city.

When you have obtained the kingdom over Idumea, when, in your body—where iniquity abounded—grace abounds still more (Romans 5), take care not to presume upon your own strength and trust that you can accomplish these things. For human glory is not certain but vain. Rather, crying out to the Lord, say with all the saints: “Give us help in tribulation, for human salvation is vain.” In you, Lord, we will act valiantly, because you will reduce to nothing all who trouble us, you who reign throughout all ages. Amen.

# PSALM 60

For the end; with hymns; a psalm of David.

Hear, God, my supplication; attend to my prayer. From the ends of the earth I cried to you when my heart was anxious; on a rock you exalted me. You led me, because you became my hope, a tower of strength in the face of the enemy. I will dwell in your tabernacle forever; I will be protected under the shelter of your wings. For you, my God, have heard my prayer; you have given an inheritance to those who fear your name.

You will add days upon days to the king; his years will extend to the day of generation and generation. He remains forever in the sight of God; who will seek out his mercy and truth? Thus I will sing a psalm to your name forever and ever, so that I may fulfill my vows from day to day.

## COMMENTARY

No one is unaware that the Church is founded upon the solidity of the rock and made a tower of strength, in which vows are rendered to God from day to day.

But you, lover of eternal life, if you wish your supplication to be heard; if you wish that, when your heart has become anxious and you have departed from the body, the Lord may appear to you as a tower of strength in the face of the enemy; if you wish to dwell in his tabernacle forever; if you wish to be protected under the shelter of his wings; if you wish to receive the inheritance obtained by those who fear his name; if you wish him to add days upon days to your years as king, so that he may bestow eternal life upon you and you may remain forever in the sight of God—seek his mercy and truth with urgency.

And after you have made them dear friends and possessed them as the hope, so to speak, of your life, sing thus to the Lord God throughout the age, even while placed in the valley of miseries. And, as though beginning each day to love them, fulfill your vows from day to day to the Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM 61

For the end; for Jeduthun; a psalm of David.

Will not my soul be subject to God? For from him comes my salvation. For he is also my God and my savior, my protector; I will no longer be moved. How long will you rush upon a man? You kill all of you, like a leaning wall and a broken-down fence. Yet they planned to drive away my price; I ran in thirst. With their mouths they blessed, but in their hearts they cursed.

Yet be subject to God, my soul, because from him comes my patience. For he is my God and my savior, my helper; I will not depart. In God is my salvation and my glory, the God of my help, and my hope is in God.

Hope in God, all the assembly of the people; pour out your hearts before him. God is our helper forever. Yet the sons of men are vain, the sons of men are liars on the scales, so that they may deceive one another through vanity. Do not hope in iniquity, and do not desire robberies. If riches flow in, do not set your heart upon them.

God has spoken once; I have heard these two things: power belongs to God, and to you, Lord, belongs mercy, because you will repay each one according to his works.

## COMMENTARY

In all the psalms the mystical sense overflows, but I am more earnestly concerned with moral explanation, in which the purpose is that we should do what we sing.

Thus, in the disposition in which your soul is subject to God, remain so fixed and solid that you may no longer be moved. When unclean spirits come to you and wish to separate you from the service of the Lord, bringing you evil opportunities and very wicked thoughts, say to them: “God is my helper; through him I will no longer be moved.”

“But how long do you rush upon human beings?” Like a wall, you fall upon all of us, and you wish either to drive my honor from me or to make my worth cheap. And when I thirst for a holy purpose and run thirsting toward it, you bless with your mouth—that is, you bring suggestions under the appearance of good counsel—but you curse with your heart: that is, you prove the thing you call good with your mouth to be evil and harmful to me.

Let us listen attentively to this passage. Demons give us good counsels full of deceit: “Let us buy and resell, and distribute the profits to the poor.” Is this not apparently good? Yet it does not allow you to enter into the powers of the Lord through this action.

Again: “Let us put aside present money; who knows what may happen?” This too appears good, but it does not make one a disciple of Christ.

Again: “Let us provide comfort to that young widow better than others do.” This too is good, but it is full of the devil’s deceits.

When demons bless you with their mouths in these and many similar matters, they curse with their hearts. Therefore say to them: “In God my savior is my glory. I will not depart from my purpose, by which I have decided to despise you.”

And say to my brothers: “Hope in him, all the gathering of my people. Pour out your hearts before him, because God is our helper.”

To those who listen to the counsels of wicked spirits speak in this manner: “Come, sons of men, liars on the scales; why do you agree with one another with your enemies? Do not hope in iniquity, because it deceives those who hope in it. Do not desire robbery, because the desire to steal kills its lover. If riches flow in, do not set your heart upon them, because greed is the root of all evils” (1 Timothy 6).

Listen carefully to this one thing that he has spoken once, because power belongs to God, and by God’s decision we obtain mercy, because he will repay each one according to his works.

But if you should seek where the Lord spoke these very words, recognize it. In Deuteronomy it is sung: “For I am God; I kill and I make alive; I strike, and I heal, and there is no one who can deliver from my hand” (Deuteronomy 32). This, therefore, is the power of God—the power of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit—who reigns throughout the ages. Amen.

# PSALM 62

A psalm of David when he was in the desert of Idumea.

God, my God, I keep watch for you from the light of dawn. My soul thirsted for you; how greatly my flesh thirsted for you. In a desert, pathless and without water, I appeared before you in the holy place, so that I might see your power and your glory. For your mercy is better than lives; my lips will praise you.

Thus I will bless you in my life, and in your name I will lift up my hands. May my soul be filled as with fat and richness, and my mouth will praise you with lips of exultation. Thus I remembered you upon my bed; in the mornings I will meditate upon you, because you have been my helper. And under the shelter of your wings I will exult; my soul clung after you, and your right hand received me.

But they sought my soul in vain; they will enter into the lower parts of the earth. They will be handed over to the hands of the sword; they will be portions for foxes. But the king will rejoice; all who swear by him will be praised in God, because the mouth of those speaking iniquity has been stopped.

## COMMENTARY

Throughout the Psalter you will nowhere find, “I will pray to you, Lord,” at any other hour except the morning—at dawn. By saying this he does not indicate merely a time, but rather that, after the night of sins has passed and the deceit of darkness has been expelled, one ceases to sleep, strives to keep watch, and, receiving the beginning of your light as though at dawn, begins to thirst for the Lord, not only in spirit but also in body, so as to see his power and his glory.

Then he recognizes that his mercy is better than life. With lips cleansed from deceit he praises the Lord, asking that this may happen to him as long as he lives, so that he may bless the Lord in his life. In the likeness of Christ’s cross, let him raise his hands, so that his soul may be filled as with fat and richness. Let him become fat in the love of God, and let his lips, full of exultation, praise his name—not compelled by necessity, but drawn by benefits.

This happens to him if he remembers God upon his bed. While another remembers lust, I, remembering God, will meditate upon him in the mornings, because he is my helper. By saying “upon my bed” and adding “helper,” he shows that by God’s assistance he was able to obtain chastity.

He then follows with the order in which he obtains help. Demons seek to seize the soul through the excess of lust. But hear what this man says: “In vain,” he says, “they sought my soul.” He explains by what means he was not captured: “I hoped under the shelter of your wings; my soul clung after you; your right hand received me.”

And so it happened that they sought my soul in vain; rather, they themselves fled while seeking me. “They entered into the lower parts of the earth”; they reached as far as the lower parts of the body. There they found the sword of the word of God, most powerful upon the thigh, and there they were handed over to the hands of the sword.

Here the lover of chastity indicates the order by which chastity is guarded. Those who seek your soul reach the lower parts of your earth; but if you have immediately girded the sword upon your thigh, you send them away with this sword by your hand to their portions.

It should properly be noted that the portions made from them are portions not of birds or dogs but of foxes, because dogs and birds are accustomed to lose their portions. Foxes act so cunningly that they not only do not lose their own, but even presume to seize those of others stronger than themselves.

Indeed, the *Physiologus* reports that the fox is always lying in wait for the wolf, so that whenever it senses that the wolf has hidden prey, it may snatch it away. Thus you too, lover of chastity, should not merely preserve your own chastity; you should also rescue, by whatever skill you can, those whom he has made his prey, so that your cunning, like that of a fox, may snatch away the demons’ portions, while chastity eats and consumes them in these deeds.

Your king, Christ the Son of God, will rejoice in the Father and the Holy Spirit, and everyone who swears by him will be praised—not by an oath made to satisfy a human being, but by preserving the laws that are in him. When this has been done, the mouth of those speaking iniquity is stopped. The demons will no longer dare to speak useless things to your heart, through the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM 63

For the end; a psalm of David.

Hear, God, my prayer when I plead; deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy. You have protected me from the assembly of the malicious, from the multitude of those who work iniquity. For they sharpened their tongues; they bent their bow against a bitter matter, so that they might shoot the blameless in secret. Suddenly they will shoot him and will not fear; they have established an evil word for themselves. They recounted how they might hide snares; they said, “Who will see them?”

They searched out iniquities; they failed while searching with scrutiny. A person will approach the deep heart, and God will be exalted. The arrows of little ones became their wounds, and their tongues were weakened against them. All who saw them were troubled, and every person feared. And they proclaimed the works of God and understood his deeds.

The righteous will rejoice in the Lord, and will hope in him, and all upright in heart will be praised.

## COMMENTARY

Hear, God, my prayer when I am afflicted or when I plead. What prayer? “Deliver my soul,” he says, “from the fear of the enemy,” you who have protected me from the assembly of the malicious and from the multitude of those who work iniquity.

You, Lord, deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy, for it has received the Holy Spirit into itself. But these people stand in secret, prepared with arrows on a bitter bow, acting so that they may shoot the blameless in secret.

Yet if a person does not consent, even if they shoot him, he will not fear. He does not withdraw; he stands manfully so that, though wounded, he may recover his health.

But they affirm an unjust word for themselves, in which they strive to hide snares. Hear what they say: “We are invisible to them; they will not see us.” And therefore they search human hearts with wicked evasions, but by the grace of God they fail in their scrutiny.

Seeing that they have failed and that a human being is approaching a higher degree of righteousness, they make his heart deep, so that through the elation of his heart God may exult apart from him [the printed reading is uncertain]. Therefore, whatever strength for despising them grows within you, O Psalmist, let the height of your heart decrease proportionately. Persevere, because “everyone who exalts himself will be humbled” (Matthew 23).

Then the arrows of little ones become their wounds. Power will be given even to your little desires, which are in Christ. To the little spiritual desires, I say, newly born from you, strength will be given, so that with their arrows they may inflict wounds upon the demons. Regarding them as nothing, they will make their tongues turn against them—that is, they will cause the things they suggested to return against them.

For just as, if we consent, we wound them, so under this rule every person who recognizes us acting will fear God, proclaim his works, and understand his deeds.

But the righteous person will not be saddened by adversities; he will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him, and he will be a praise to all who are upright in heart, in Christ our Lord, who reigns throughout the ages. Amen.

# PSALM 64

For the end; a psalm; a song of Haggai, Jeremiah, and Ezekiel, concerning the word of the pilgrimage and concerning the people of the transmigration, when they began to set out.

Praise is fitting for you, God, in Zion, and the vow will be paid to you in Jerusalem. Hear my prayer; all flesh will come to you. The words of the wicked have prevailed over us, but you will be gracious toward our impieties.

Blessed is the one whom you have chosen and taken up; he will dwell in your courts. We will be filled with the good things of your house; your temple is holy, wondrous in righteousness.

Hear us, God our savior, hope of all the ends of the earth and of the distant sea. You prepare the mountains by your strength, girded with power; you trouble the depths of the sea and the sound of its waves. The nations will be troubled, and those who inhabit the ends of the earth will fear because of your signs. You will delight the outlets of morning and evening.

You have visited the earth and intoxicated it; you have multiplied its wealth and made it rich. The river of God is filled with waters; you have prepared their food, for such is your preparation. Watering its streams, multiply its produce; in its drops the sprouting land will rejoice.

You will bless the crown of the year of your kindness, and your fields will be filled with abundance. The beautiful places of the desert will grow fat, and the hills will gird themselves with exultation. The rams have clothed themselves with sheep, and the valleys will abound with grain; indeed, they will cry out and sing a hymn.

## COMMENTARY

In the Hebrew it contains neither Jeremiah nor Haggai, but David alone. But Ezra, having affection for them, wished to mention them, asserting that David sang this psalm concerning them at the beginning of their prophecy: “This is outside the foreign land, and he cannot sing hymns in a foreign land.”

Let our soul, therefore, be Zion, so that a hymn may fittingly be sung in it. It will be Zion if it fulfills the vow it made to Jerusalem—if it fulfills the vow it made to God, namely, to renounce the devil and his pomp. Then God hears its prayer, when all flesh comes to him. For there is neither tribe nor nation from which the knee will not be bent to the Lord Jesus Christ.

When the apostles preached, “their sound went out into all the earth” (Philippians 2). And although the words of the wicked—namely, of the Pharisees—prevailed against them and afflicted them impiously, he says: “You will be gracious toward the impieties that we suffer.”

For blessed is the Lord Jesus Christ, whom you chose and took up. He dwelt in your tabernacles when you filled him with the good things of your house, in which your holy temple reigns—not made by hands, but begotten by the Word and brought forth from a virgin womb. To him we say: “Hear us, God our savior.” For you gave hope to the entire human race, both to those who are far away and to those who are near.

When you prepared the mountains by your strength, to which you said, “Preach the Gospel to every creature” (Matthew 16), you said that these signs would be shown to believers: “You will heal the sick, illuminate the blind, and raise the dead.”

By these signs the nations were troubled, and all who inhabit the ends of the earth feared God. For from these signs the fear of God took its beginning upon the face of the earth.

And God will delight in the outlet of morning and evening—that is, in the East and the West, in the building of the churches. You will delight there because you visited the earth by your coming and intoxicated it with your blood, when the river Jordan was filled with waters—namely, with the voices of the prophets.

Then you prepared food, not food that perishes, because such is your preparation. You intoxicated its streams, so that, when it was the third hour of the day, they were thought to be drunk.

At the time when you multiplied its generations—whose generations? That is, those of the Jordan, which is baptism—there were Parthians, Medes, and Elamites, Cretans, Syrians, Arabs, Romans, and Cyrenians, and nearly all the nations from whom you multiplied its generations when it began to rise like heavenly drops.

Then the crown of the year began with the holy day of Easter, and the fields were filled with abundance. Everything rejoices in fertility and feasts in celebration, so that the ends of the desert grow fat and the hills gird themselves with exultation.

For the rams will be clothed with the gentleness of sheep; they will not strike with their horns, and the valleys will abound with the grain of Christ’s body. When they receive it, the rams and the sheep together will cry out, singing a hymn to Christ the Son of God, who reigns with the Father and the Holy Spirit, in the unity of the Godhead and in the Trinity of unity, throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

# PSALM 65

For the end; a song of the psalm of the Resurrection.

Shout joyfully to God, all the earth; sing a psalm to his name; give glory to his praise. Say to God: “How fearsome are your works, Lord! In the abundance of your strength your enemies will lie to you.” All the earth will worship you, God, and sing psalms to you; it will sing a psalm to your name.

Come and see the works of God, fearsome in his counsels concerning the sons of men. He turned the sea into dry land; they crossed the river on foot. There we rejoiced in him, who rules in his strength forever. His eyes look upon the nations; let those who provoke him not exalt themselves in themselves.

Bless our God, nations; make the voice of his praise heard. He has appointed my soul for life and has not allowed my feet to be shaken. For you have tested us, God; you have examined us by fire, as silver is examined. You led us into a snare; you placed tribulations upon our back; you set human beings over our heads. We passed through fire and water, and you led us out into refreshment.

I will enter your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to you, vows which my lips have uttered. And my mouth spoke in my tribulation. I will offer you burnt offerings rich in marrow; with the incense of rams I will offer to you bulls with goats.

Come and hear, and I will tell all who fear God how much he has done for my soul. I cried out to him with my mouth, and I rejoiced under my tongue [the printed reading *lingna* is evidently corrupt; the sense is “under my tongue”]. If I had seen iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have heard.

Therefore God heard and attended to the voice of my supplication. Blessed is God, who has not removed my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

## COMMENTARY
The land of the Jews alone once rejoiced to God; but because now his eyes—that is, God’s eyes—look upon the nations through Christ, Judaea no longer alone rejoices to God. Rather, the whole earth sings a psalm to God’s name, gives glory to his praise, and says to God: “For your works are fearsome in the abundance of your power,” by which you declared yourself the true God, the Son, when your enemies lied, saying, “He is not from God” (John 8), while you were driving out demons, raising the dead, cleansing lepers, healing paralytics, walking upon the sea, and commanding the winds.

In this abundance of your power your enemies lied to you, saying, “We know that you are from God, and you do not accept people’s persons” (John 3). Yet they lied still more in the abundance of your power when they said that you had been stolen by your disciples after you had already risen, and the whole earth—in whose heart you had been—was worshiping you. They said to the soldiers, “Lie; say that he was stolen while you were sleeping” (Matthew 28). This psalm announces the resurrection in its title: do not lie. If you were sleeping, you did not see who carried away the body. Either you saw those carrying it away and were not sleeping, or you were sleeping and did not see. Why do you lie?

Rather, come and see the works of the Lord. He is the one who turned the sea into dry land, so that your fathers might cross through the midst of the sea on dry ground. He is the one who divided the river, so that your fathers might cross it on foot. Rather, all of you rejoice together, because he is the one who rules in his power forever. And because his eyes look upon the nations, you Jews, rejoice that the promise of your Father is being fulfilled. For God said to Abraham, “In your seed I will inherit all the nations” (Genesis 22).

Why are you jealous of them, and, in your customary manner, provoke the Lord to anger, so that he says to you, “The kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing his will” (Matthew 21)? Therefore, nations, bless our God and obey the voice of his praise. The Church follows this in all things, together with the apostles and martyrs.

“He set my soul toward life,” it says, “and did not allow my feet to be shaken,” when you tested us, God, and examined us by fire, as silver is examined. You led us into a snare, laid tribulations upon our back, and placed people above our heads. Yet we passed through the fire of martyrdom and the water of baptism, and you led us into refreshment.

For in baptism we were marked with the Holy Spirit and fire, when we entered your house with burnt offerings and fulfilled the vows that our mouth had uttered in our tribulation. “I will offer you sacrifices rich in marrow.” Let him offer God sacrifices without marrow who is empty in heart, though he appears to pray and sing psalms bodily. But I, he says, will offer you sacrifices rich in marrow: “I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray also with the mind; I will sing psalms with the spirit, and I will sing psalms also with the mind” (1 Corinthians 14).

“I will offer the incense of rams”: bravely resisting, in zeal for your sheep, every heretic. “I will offer you bulls” when I preach; “goats” when I bring the rule of lust under control, or slaughter it.

“Come and hear how much God has done for my soul.” To rescue my soul, he laid down his own soul; to rescue me from death, he accepted death. If I do not believe that you are the true God, and you see in my heart the wickedness of one who denies this, do not hear me, God. But because I believe that you are, therefore you have heard me. I bless you, who have not removed my prayer from me, nor your mercy from me, who reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

[Col. 0415D]

## PSALM 66

For the end; with hymns, a psalm of a song, of David.

May God have mercy on us and bless us; may he make his face shine upon us and have mercy on us, so that we may know your way on earth and your salvation among all nations. Let the peoples confess to you, God; let all the peoples confess to you. Let the nations rejoice and exult, because you judge the peoples with equity and guide the nations on earth. Let the peoples confess to you, God; let all the peoples confess to you: the earth has yielded its fruit. May God, our God, bless us; may God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him.

[Col. 0416A]

### Commentary

“In hymns, a psalm of a song” refers to what the angels sang: “Glory in the highest” (Matthew 2), when he came, making his face shine upon us, and blessed us so that we might know the way of God on earth and his salvation among all nations.

Let the peoples confess this, because you came so that the nations might rejoice, because they are beginning to be governed by your judgment in equity, and on the earth of their own body they are being removed from perversity and guided along a straight course.

Let all the peoples confess this also, because Mary, from an earthly body but with a heavenly seed, gave her fruit, so that the fruit itself might bless in the Trinity.

“May God bless us, our God; may God bless us.” God is named three times, yet the one in the Trinity is named—the one whom all the ends of the earth fear—through all ages of ages. Amen.

[Col. 0416B]

## PSALM 67

For the end; a psalm of a song, of David.

Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his face. As smoke vanishes, so may they vanish; as wax melts before the fire, so may sinners perish before the face of God. But let the righteous feast and exult in the sight of God, and delight in gladness.

Sing to God; sing a psalm to his name; make a way for him who ascends above the setting sun—the Lord is his name. Exult in his sight; they will be troubled before him, the father of orphans and judge of widows. God is in his holy place; God makes those of one mind dwell in a house. He brings out prisoners in strength, and likewise those who provoke him, who dwell in tombs.

God, when you go out before your people, when you pass through the desert, the earth was shaken; indeed, the heavens dripped before the face of Sinai, before the face of the God of Israel. You will set apart a willing rain, God, for your inheritance; and it was weakened, but you perfected it. Your animals will dwell in it; in your sweetness you prepared it for the poor, God.

The Lord will give the word to those evangelizing with great power. The King of the powers of the Beloved, and the beauty of the house, to divide spoils. If you sleep among the middle divisions, the wings of a silvered dove, and the rear parts of its back in the pallor of gold. While the heavenly one distinguishes kings over it, they will be whitened with snow in Selmon.

The mountain of God is a rich mountain, a curdled mountain, a rich mountain. Why do you suspect the curdled mountains? The mountain in which it pleased the Lord to dwell, for the Lord has dwelt there forever.

The chariot of God is multiplied ten thousandfold, thousands upon thousands of rejoicing ones. The Lord is among them, at Sinai, in the holy place. You ascended on high, you took captivity captive, you received gifts among human beings. Indeed, even the unbelievers, so that the Lord God might dwell.

Blessed be the Lord day by day. God will make our way prosperous, the God of our salvation. Our God is the God who saves, and the exits of the Lord, the Lord, are from death.

Yet God will crush the heads of his enemies, the crown of the hair of those who walk in their sins. The Lord said: “From Bashan I will turn back; I will turn back into the depth of the sea.” So that your foot may be dipped in blood, and the tongue of your dogs in it, from the enemies, by him.

They saw your processions, God, the processions of my God, my king, who is in the holy place. Princes went before, joined to those singing in the midst of young women playing tambourines. In the churches bless God the Lord, from the springs of Israel.

There is Benjamin, the youngest, in ecstasy of mind. The princes of Judah are their leaders; the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali. Command, God, your power; strengthen, God, what you have worked in us. From your temple in Jerusalem kings will offer you gifts.

Rebuke the beasts of the reed, the assembly of bulls among the calves of the peoples, so that they may exclude those who have been tested as silver. Scatter the nations that desire wars. Ambassadors will come from Egypt; Ethiopia will hasten to stretch out its hand to God.

Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing psalms to the Lord. Sing psalms to God, who ascends above the heaven of heaven toward the east. Behold, he will give his voice a voice of power. Give glory to God over Israel; his magnificence and power are in the clouds.

God is wondrous in his holy ones. The God of Israel himself will give power and strength to his people. Blessed be God.

[Col. 0417B]

### Commentary

This is likewise a psalm of a song in which he rises from the dead, so that his enemies may be scattered and those who crucified him may flee from his face. As smoke vanishes while rising against the heights, so may they vanish; and as wax melts, feeling the fire but returning to its own nature, so may sinners perish without the sight of God.

But let these—that is, the apostles—when the Lord has risen, feast and delight in gladness. Until he ascends above the setting sun, let them make a way for him and rejoice in his sight. He ascended above the setting sun because, at his setting, the world began to be when he ascended into the heavens. Hence the apostle John also says: “Children, it is the last hour” (1 John 2).

The Jews were troubled before his face when he showed himself to be the father of orphans and judge of widows. “God is in his holy place.” Wherever holiness is, there is God’s place, and there God is. He himself makes people of one mind in the house—in his Church, certainly—to practice one complete faith. He himself will bring out those imprisoned by the devil in his strength.

And those who provoke him to anger—that is, those who serve magical arts—are the ones who dwell in tombs.

“God, go out before your people.” When you passed through the desert, you changed the earth, when the heavens brought forth the star, before the face of the God of Israel. Then, God, you set apart a willing rain for your inheritance, when the angels sang: “Peace to people of good will” (Matthew 2).

His inheritance began among the apostles. In them that inheritance was weakened, but the Lord himself perfected it by rising from the dead, showing the fissures of the nails in his hands and the sign of the wound in his side. He perfected it in such a way that not only spiritual but also natural human beings dwell in it, because God prepared his sweetness for them when the Lord gave the word to the women, so that they might evangelize with great power.

The Lord therefore gave them the word, saying: “Go, tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me” (Matthew 28).

Who said this? “The King of the powers of the Beloved”—that is, the inner reality of Christ—and “the beauty of the house,” namely, the beautiful form of his body, beautiful above the sons of human beings. In it he divides spoils: he took the synagogue captive and divided its treasures in the Church. To one he gave prophecy, to another the word, to another the power of healings. In short, the synagogue no longer possesses either a prophet, or anointing, or sacrifice. These are the spoils taken from the captive synagogue, divided while the scribes and Pharisees slept among the middle divisions.

“Among the middle divisions,” I say—that is, among the holy books. The Jews and many of our interpreters alike say that *cleros* means books in this passage.

Therefore, if you sleep—that is, neglect—while placed among the divine books, and, holding the keys of the kingdom, neither enter yourselves nor permit others to enter, you are the “wings of a silvered dove”—that is, you wings of a silvered dove, pretending to the dove’s simplicity, as though you were its wings.

Yet you are silvered wings, not true silver, and you display the appearance of gold, not true gold.

Therefore, if you sleep, I will set up heavenly kings who are watchful—that is, the apostles—over the earth, so that their sound may go out into all the earth. Thus those whom the blackness of sins has seized will, at their preaching, be whitened like snow in Selmon.

Selmon is the place where proselytes were purified, or where those who confessed themselves defiled by more serious pollutions were purified. *Κατ’ ἀντίφρασιν*—“by contrariety” or “ironical reversal”—he wished Selmon to be understood as every place in which those blackened by the filth of sins are whitened.

Therefore, when the Lord distinguishes his apostles over the earth, whoever heard them and believed—if they had been black [the source’s *fenisecium* is uncertain]—became like white wool and, as though whitened by snow, were made white in Selmon, in the place of purification where all sins are washed away.

There is the mountain of God, a rich mountain: no other than Christ Jesus himself, rich, sweating with the oil of righteousness, the oil of chrism. He is a curdled mountain. This same rich mountain, in the unity of the Godhead, bears the Trinity curdled together.

See that you do not receive one person of the Godhead from another. For those who do this are reproved, and it is said to them: “Why do you receive rich mountains in this way?” That is: Why do you make the Godhead plural? Hold the curdled mountain in unity, and contemplate the Father and the Holy Spirit in our one Lord Jesus Christ.

For he is the mountain in which it pleased God to dwell, and in him the Lord dwelt throughout the ages of ages.

“His chariot is ten thousandfold.” His multiplied chariot was driven in the Passion, where he himself was more than sufficient for himself than ten thousand legions of angels and the thousands of rejoicing ones who were with Moses at Sinai in the holy place.

Then he ascended on high—that is, onto the cross. He took captivity captive: he took captivity itself, the captivity of the first tree, and condemned sin by means of sin. From the wood of the cross, I say, he seized the wood of desire, and distributed gifts to human beings.

He also suffered for those who did not believe, and even to them, while placed upon the cross, he gave gifts—and not small gifts. Hear how great they were: he poured out prayers for them, saying, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing” (Luke 23).

Thus he gave gifts to human beings—that is, to believers—and not only to believers, but also to those who do not believe that the Lord dwells in them, who do not believe “that God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself” (2 Corinthians 5).

Blessed be the Lord the Father; blessed be God the Son; blessed be the Lord the Holy Spirit, because God our Savior made the way of his cross prosperous for us. For this reason he wished to be crucified, so that he might save us. For this reason he accepted the destruction of death, so that he might crush the heads of his enemies and free sinners from the hands of demons, who were walking from the crown of their hair in their sins.

The Lord said: “From Bashan I will turn back.” Bashan was a king who took Israel captive on account of sin. Therefore, those who were taken captive by Bashan because of their sins I will turn back from Bashan through my cross.

But because the devil’s dwelling is in the abysses and in the deep, I will turn back even from there, says the perfect inner Godhead, surely speaking to his human being, Jesus Christ. “I will turn back,” he says, “even from the depth of the sea,” until your foot is dipped in the blood of the Passion.

There the tongue of your dogs—that is, of the barking dogs—said, “Crucify, crucify” (Luke 23). Therefore, this tongue of dogs was stirred up against him by the devil himself.

But after the Passion, your processions were seen, God. It was proved that God had entered into a human being, and that he is in the holy place. Of him the princes, the prophets, went before, joined with the women singing in the midst of young women who had gone out to meet David, singing: “David has conquered among ten thousand” (1 Samuel 18).

After Goliath had been cast down, Christ in David was victorious there in the midst of the young women playing tambourines. But because there was an image there, the truth is established here.

Do not sing these things in the synagogues, but in the churches of the holy. There bless the Lord—not one who comes from elsewhere, not a stranger, not a new deity, but the one who always is, the Lord from the springs of Israel.

There is Benjamin, the younger, in fear. Where? There, undoubtedly, in the churches. There is that Benjamin who says, “I am an Israelite from the tribe of Benjamin” (Romans 11). Why “younger”? Because he was born last to his father.

Among those eleven he began to be the twelfth, but at the banquet he received a double portion, so that, laboring more than all of them, he attributed this very labor not to himself but to the grace of his Father God.

There, therefore, is Benjamin, the younger, in fear—that is, in ecstasy of mind. For he suddenly fell and was terrified; he fell to the earth and rose in heaven; he fell as a persecutor and rose as an apostle; Saul fell and Paul rose.

Yet where, where is Benjamin? Where, if you ask? “There,” he says, “where are the princes of Judah, where are the princes of Zebulun, where are the princes of Naphtali; where God commanded his power; where he confirmed what he worked in us; where is the temple raised in three days, which is in Jerusalem; where kings offer gifts; where the beasts of the forest are rebuked.”

Heretics are those who, like beasts in the forest, cherish a hiding place in the forest of the law, so that from concealment they may injure the council of the bulls among the calves of the peoples.

For they strive to injure the counsels of the priests, who in this passage are called bulls, fit for the altar among calves—that is, among deaf and ignorant peoples who live among them.

Why, then, are they requested to be rebuked by God? So that their foolishness may become known to everyone, lest, if they are not rebuked, they exclude those who are not silvered but have been tested as silver.

Scatter, Lord, those who desire wars. Ambassadors will come from Egypt. With Pharaoh drowned, send your leaders to Egypt; let them act as ambassadors from Egypt. Let your hand also precede Ethiopia, the inner part of Egypt itself, so that the kingdoms of the earth may sing to you, who ascended into the heavens of heavens toward the East, when you gave your voice, a voice of power, so that in your name the apostles might receive the power to command over all the sick, over demons, and over death itself.

Performing these signs, they would say to the nations: “Give honor to God; his name is great over Israel,” and through him who sees God in Christ, whose power is in the clouds—that is, in the apostles. When sending them to the nations, he warned them not to rain upon the Jew, so that he might fulfill what he said: “I will command my clouds not to rain rain upon her” (Isaiah 5).

For he no longer wishes to be wondrous among unbelievers, although he was always wondrous among unbelievers; rather, he is now wondrous in his holy ones. To those who believe he gives power, and through them he gives strength to his people. Blessed is God, who reigns throughout the ages of ages. Amen.

## PSALM 68

[Col. 0420B]

For the end; for those who will be changed; a psalm of David.

Save me, God, because the waters have entered as far as my soul. I am stuck in the mud of the deep, and there is no firm ground. I have come into the depth of the sea, and the storm has overwhelmed me. I have labored crying out; my throat has become hoarse; my eyes have failed while I hope in my God.

Those who hate me without cause have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head. My enemies, who unjustly persecute me, have grown strong; what I did not steal, I then had to repay.

God, you know my foolishness, and my offenses are not hidden from you. Let those who wait for you, Lord of hosts, not be put to shame because of me. Let those who seek you, God of Israel, not be confounded because of me.

For on your account I endured reproach; shame covered my face. I became a stranger to my brothers and an alien to the sons of my mother. For zeal for your house consumed me, and the reproaches of those reproaching you fell upon me.

I covered my soul in fasting, and it became a reproach to me. I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a proverb to them. Those sitting at the gate spoke against me, and those drinking wine sang derisively about me.

But I, my prayer was to you, Lord, at an acceptable time, God. In the abundance of your mercy hear me, according to the truth of your salvation. Rescue me from the mud, so that I may not become stuck; deliver me from those who hate me and from the depths of the waters.

Do not let the storm of water overwhelm me, nor let the deep swallow me, nor let the pit close its mouth over me. Hear me, Lord, because your mercy is kind; according to the abundance of your compassions, look upon me.

Do not turn your face away from your servant, because I am troubled; hear me quickly. Attend to my soul and deliver it; because of my enemies rescue me.

You know my reproach, my confusion, and my reverence. All those who trouble me are before you. My heart awaited reproach and misery. I waited for one who would grieve with me, but there was none; for one who would console me, but I found none.

They gave gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. Let their table before them become a snare, and a retribution and a stumbling-block. Let their eyes be darkened so that they may not see, and always make their back bent.

Pour out your anger upon them, and let the fury of your anger seize them. Let their dwelling become desolate, and let there be no one dwelling in their tents.

For the one whom you struck, they persecuted, and they added to the pain of my wounds. Add iniquity upon their iniquity, and let them not enter into your righteousness. Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.

I am poor and suffering; your salvation, God, has received me. I will praise the name of God with a song, and magnify him with praise. It will please God more than a young calf producing horns and hooves.

Let the poor see and rejoice; seek God, and your soul will live. For the Lord has heard the poor and has not despised his prisoners. Let the heavens and earth praise him, the sea and all the creeping things in them.

For God will save Zion, and the cities of Judah will be built. They will dwell there and acquire it as an inheritance. The seed of his servants will possess it, and those who love his name will dwell in it.

[Col. 0421B]

### Commentary

In our Lord Jesus Christ we confess two substances, of God and of human being, attributing the powers to God and applying the weaknesses to the human being. We recognize his voice prophesied throughout this psalm, from beginning to end.

Human speech has the custom that, when someone suffers a serious accusation, we say that he lies down under a severe storm. In this manner he signifies that the waters have reached his soul.

By saying that he is stuck in the mud of the deep, he refers to the structure of the first human being, in which the storm of the rebellious people, fixed to the cross, plunged him into death.

Now he asks for his disciples, so that those who await his resurrection may not be ashamed in him, nor those who seek you in me, God of Israel, be confounded.

“For your sake,” he says, “I bore reproach. While I was doing your will, I offended them.” Reverence covered my face, struck with blows; I became a stranger to my brothers, for all abandoned me and fled.
